CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_S_Ent_Folder_Rev]
(@ent_id     INT32_NULL = NULL,
@oper_id    STRING40 = NULL,
@item_id    STRING40 = NULL,
@wo_id      STRING40 = NULL,
@seq_no     INT32 = NULL,
@job_pos    INT32 = 0)
AS
--- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name	      -	SP_S_ENT_FOLDER_REV
-- Description	      -	Using the entity id recursively check through the chain of parent entity id if a folder exists
-- Author             -       Sheetal Jain
-- Date Created	      -	01/27/2003
-- Version	      -       1.5.0.1
--
-- Copyright (c) 2017 Schneider Electric Software, LLC. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Date_Modified  Modified_By     Ver   	Changes
--02/13/2003	Raghu		1.5.5	If no folder records exists/found, then return an empty recordset to the client apps
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- *************************************************************************************************************************
SET NOCOUNT ON
DECLARE
  @V_Found       CHAR(1),
  @V_Ent         INT32,
  @V_Folder_Ver  STRING40_NULL,
  @V_Process     STRING40,
  @V_Wo_Id       STRING40,
  @V_Oper_Id     STRING40,
  @V_Seq_No      INT32,
  @V_Item        STRING40
BEGIN
  SET @V_Found = 'N'
  SET @V_Ent = @ent_id
  SET @V_Wo_Id = @wo_id
  SET @V_Oper_Id = @oper_id
  SET @V_Seq_No = @seq_no
  SET @V_Item = @item_id
  IF @wo_id IS NOT NULL  --Get the process
    SELECT @V_Process = process_id FROM wo WHERE wo_id = @wo_id
  --Get the folder revision and process
  IF @oper_id IS NOT NULL AND @wo_id IS NOT NULL AND @seq_no IS NOT NULL
    SELECT @V_Folder_Ver = folder_ver_id FROM job WHERE wo_id = @wo_id AND oper_id = @oper_id AND seq_no = @seq_no

  --Recursively check for folder until found
  WHILE @V_Found = 'N'
  BEGIN
    --Get the folder revision and process
    IF @oper_id IS NULL OR @item_id IS NULL OR @wo_id IS NULL OR @seq_no IS NULL
    BEGIN
      SET @V_Wo_Id = NULL
      SET @V_Oper_Id = NULL
      SET @V_Seq_No = NULL
      SET @V_Item = NULL
      --Get the current wo, operation and seq
      SELECT @V_Wo_Id = cur_wo_id, @V_Oper_Id = cur_oper_id, @V_Seq_No = cur_seq_no FROM job_exec WHERE ent_id = @V_Ent AND job_pos = @job_pos
      --Get the item being produced at this operation
      IF @V_Wo_Id IS NOT NULL AND @V_Oper_Id IS NOT NULL AND @V_Seq_No IS NOT NULL
      BEGIN
        SELECT @V_Item = item_id, @V_Folder_Ver = folder_ver_id FROM job WHERE wo_id = @V_Wo_Id AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND seq_no = @V_Seq_No
        SELECT @V_Process = process_id FROM wo WHERE wo_id = @V_Wo_Id
      END
    END
    --operation and item provided
    IF @V_Item IS NOT NULL
    BEGIN
      IF 1 = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent)
      BEGIN  --  Only one folder record found
        SELECT item_id, oper_id, ent_id, ver_id, oper_desc, notes, udf1, udf2,
		preferred_ver, design_hold, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by,
		last_edit_at, CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, mod_id))) mod_id,
		row_id
	FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent
        SET @V_Found = 'Y'
      END
      ELSE  -- Select the version specified in job
      BEGIN
        IF @V_Folder_Ver IS NOT NULL  --folder version provided
        BEGIN
          IF EXISTS (SELECT 'X' FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent AND ver_id = @V_Folder_Ver)
          BEGIN
	        SELECT item_id, oper_id, ent_id, ver_id, oper_desc, notes, udf1, udf2,
		preferred_ver, design_hold, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by,
		last_edit_at, CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, mod_id))) mod_id,
		row_id
		FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent AND ver_id = @V_Folder_Ver
            SET @V_Found = 'Y'
          END
        END  --End of @folder_ver IS NOT NULL
        IF @V_Found = 'N' AND @V_Process IS NOT NULL  -- Folder not found yet, check for default folder
        BEGIN
          IF EXISTS(SELECT 'X' FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent
            AND ver_id = (SELECT ver_id FROM folder_item_oper_ent_link WHERE process_id = @V_Process AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id
                            AND ent_id = @V_Ent ANd item_id = @V_Item))
          BEGIN  --row found
        	SELECT item_id, oper_id, ent_id, ver_id, oper_desc, notes, udf1, udf2,
		preferred_ver, design_hold, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by,
		last_edit_at, CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, mod_id))) mod_id,
		row_id
		FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent
              AND ver_id = (SELECT ver_id FROM folder_item_oper_ent_link WHERE process_id = @V_Process AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id
                            AND ent_id = @V_Ent ANd item_id = @V_Item)
            SET @V_Found = 'Y'
          END
        END --  End of @V_Found = 'N' AND @process_id IS NOT NULL
        IF @V_Found = 'N'  --  Folder not found yet, preferred folder version
        BEGIN
          IF EXISTS (SELECT 'X' FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent AND preferred_ver = 1)
          BEGIN  --row found
        	SELECT item_id, oper_id, ent_id, ver_id, oper_desc, notes, udf1, udf2,
		preferred_ver, design_hold, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by,
		last_edit_at, CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, mod_id))) mod_id,
		row_id
		FROM folder WHERE item_id = @V_Item AND oper_id = @V_Oper_Id AND ent_id = @V_Ent AND preferred_ver = 1
            SET @V_Found = 'Y'
          END
        END
      END
    END  --End of @oper_id IS NOT NULL AND @item_id IS NOT NULL
    IF @V_Found = 'N'  -- folder not found for this entity
    BEGIN
      --Check if this entity has a preferred parent
      SELECT @V_Ent = parent_ent_id FROM ent WHERE ent_id = @V_Ent
      IF @V_Ent IS NULL OR @@ROWCOUNT = 0 BEGIN
        SET @V_Found = 'Y'
        --Added by Raghu on 02/13/2003. If no records are found, return an empty recordset to the client apps
        SELECT item_id, oper_id, ent_id, ver_id, oper_desc, notes, udf1, udf2,
		preferred_ver, design_hold, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by,
		last_edit_at, CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, mod_id))) mod_id,
		row_id
	FROM folder WHERE item_id IS NULL
     END
    END  --End of @V_Found = 'N'
  END  --End of @V_Found = 'Y'
END

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_U_Sample_GenSamplesForAnEnt
(@qm_ent_id				INT32
,@ent_name				STRING80
,@event_time_utc		TDATETIME
,@spec_priority			INT32
,@sample_start_time_utc	TDATETIME
,@shift_end_time_utc	TDATETIME
,@context_ent_id		INT32
,@qm_spec_id			INT32
,@qm_spec_name			STRING80
,@plan_id				INT32
,@plan_name				STRING40
,@reset_option			INT32
,@plan_override			LOGICAL
,@qm_spec_end_eff_utc	TDATETIME
,@sample_name_template	STRING80
,@wo_id					STRING80
,@oper_id				STRING80
,@seq_no				INT32
,@item_id				STRING80
,@context_item_id		STRING80
,@item_category_id			INT32
,@process_id			STRING80
,@context_oper_id		STRING80
,@freq_id				INT32
,@freq_name				STRING40
,@freq_type				INT32
,@sample_interval_sec	TFLOAT
,@interval_unit			INT32
,@offset_start_sec		INT32
,@offset_end_sec		INT32
,@samples_per_shift		INT32
,@expiry_interval_min	INT32
,@warning_interval_min	INT32
,@user_id				STRING80
,@ready_prod_count_sample	BIT
,@prod_offset_end_sec	INT32
,@first_prod_sample_sec TFLOAT
) AS
-- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name		- sp_U_Sample_GenSamplesForAnEnt
-- Description		- The purpose of this stored procedure is to generate samples using the spec, sample plan frequencies for an entity
-- Author			- Raghu G
-- Date Created		- 01/06/2012
-- Version			- 1.0
--
-- Copyright (c) 2019 AVEVA Group Plc. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Change Date	Change By	Ver.	Changes
-- 07/03/2013	Saiteja 	4.6		CR L00127048 - Modified the SP to not generate future samples based off of Ad-hoc/manual samples.
-- 02/03/2017	RaghuG		5.3	UserStory: 754651 - MOL: As Schneider Electric, I want to merge L00143704 (HF CR L00143488: SR 19912585 An issue with the SRO object not connecting after a switchover of AOS.)
-- 09/03/2019   Raghu G		6.2     US-1191717-CR L00154065 - Merged changes for hot fix CR L00153497 by JAE on 04/30/2019: account for sample frequency offsets when generating samples for calendar frequencies
-- NOTE: All datetime examples in this stored procedure uses Eastern Time (ET)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SET NOCOUNT ON
SET XACT_ABORT ON

DECLARE  @sample_end_time_utc_offset		TDATETIME
		,@sample_requested_time_utc			TDATETIME
		,@sample_requested_time_local		TDATETIME
		,@start_time_local_offset			TDATETIME
		,@sample_end_time_utc				TDATETIME
		,@day_or_week_start					TDATETIME
		,@expiry_time_utc				TDATETIME
		,@warning_time_utc				TDATETIME

		,@sample_counter					INT32
		,@char_name							STRING80
		,@sample_name						STRING80
		,@prev_sample_name_instance					STRING80
		,@sample_id				INT32
		,@templ_name_cont_char_name		INT32

		,@curr_sample_request_time_local	TDATETIME
		,@next_sample_request_time_local	TDATETIME
		,@sample_name_instance			STRING80
		,@current_sample_no			INT32
		,@prev_sample_no			INT32
		,@context_id				INT32
		--,@ready_sample_id			INT32
		,@spare4_value				STRING80

-- The purpose of this table is to have a collection containing each characteristic that requires a sample at a given time.
-- I.E. this table contains a list of characteristics for each time bucket for which sample_to_go and sample_char_link_to_go records ought to be created.
DECLARE @sample_characteristic			TABLE(requested_time_utc DATETIME, char_id INT, existing_sample BIT, first_sample_set BIT)

-- The purpose of this table is to have a list of characteristics for which the samples are already generated/accounted for a given context
-- by a spec that is NOT the current spec.
DECLARE @chars_to_be_collected			TABLE (char_id INT, char_exists BIT)

-- The purpose of this table is to have a list of unique future samples for each time requested in the future identified by requested time, sample name and sample id.
DECLARE @unique_future_samples			TABLE (requested_time_utc DATETIME, sample_name NVARCHAR(80), sample_id INT, existing_sample BIT)

BEGIN
	--Build a list of characteristics for those require future samples, and they are not already accounted by other specs.
	IF (@freq_type = 1) -- Calendar frequency
		--Determine which characteristics are accounted by other frequencies in the char_exists column (e.g. shift, runtime, etc.)
		--If a characteristic is not accounted by any frequencies, then it is straight-forward to determine the subsequent samples for a characteristic;
		--otherwise, a characteristic has to go through each sample request times to determine when the next sample ought to be collected.
		INSERT INTO @chars_to_be_collected (char_id, char_exists)
		SELECT qscl.char_id, CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK)
							INNER JOIN sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK) ON stg.sample_id = scltg.sample_id
							WHERE stg.requested_time_utc >= @event_time_utc AND scltg.char_id = qscl.char_id)
					THEN 1
					ELSE 0 END
		FROM qm_spec_char_link qscl WITH (NOLOCK)
		INNER JOIN characteristic c WITH (NOLOCK) ON qscl.char_id = c.char_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT scltg.char_id
				 FROM sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK)
				 INNER JOIN sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK) ON stg.sample_id = scltg.sample_id
				 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
				   AND stg.requested_time_utc >= @event_time_utc AND stg.requested_time_utc < DATEADD(SS,@sample_interval_sec,@event_time_utc) -- HF L00153497
				   AND (((stg.wo_id = @wo_id OR (stg.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
				   AND (stg.oper_id = @oper_id OR (stg.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
				   AND (stg.seq_no = @seq_no OR (stg.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL)))
				   OR (stg.wo_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.oper_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.seq_no IS NOT NULL AND @spec_priority = 11))
				   AND scltg.qm_spec_id <> @qm_spec_id
				 ) chars_accntd_by_other_specs ON c.char_id = chars_accntd_by_other_specs.char_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT scltg.char_id, MIN(stg.freq_id) freq_id
				 FROM sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK)
				 INNER JOIN sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK) ON stg.sample_id = scltg.sample_id
				 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
				   AND stg.requested_time_utc >= @event_time_utc AND stg.requested_time_utc < DATEADD(SS,@sample_interval_sec,@event_time_utc) -- HF L00153497
				   AND (((stg.wo_id = @wo_id OR (stg.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
				   AND (stg.oper_id = @oper_id OR (stg.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
				   AND (stg.seq_no = @seq_no OR (stg.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL)))
				   OR (stg.wo_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.oper_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.seq_no IS NOT NULL AND @spec_priority = 11))
				   AND scltg.qm_spec_id = @qm_spec_id
				   -- HF L00153497: Commented out to prevent duplicate samples from being created
				   -- AND stg.freq_id <> @freq_id
				   GROUP BY scltg.char_id
				) chars_accntd_by_other_freq ON c.char_id = chars_accntd_by_other_freq.char_id
		WHERE qscl.qm_spec_id = @qm_spec_id
		-- Exclude the characteristics whose severity code is set to 0 (UnUsed)
		  AND COALESCE(qscl.severity_cd, c.severity_cd) > 0
		-- Retrieve all the characeristics that do not have a overidden plan_id OR
		-- the characteristics that do have the overridden plan_id and the supplied plan_id match the plan_id of a characteristics.
		 AND ((qscl.plan_id = @plan_id) OR (qscl.plan_id IS NULL AND @plan_override = 0))
		 AND chars_accntd_by_other_specs.char_id IS NULL
	ELSE
		INSERT INTO @chars_to_be_collected (char_id)
		SELECT qscl.char_id
		FROM qm_spec_char_link qscl WITH (NOLOCK)
		INNER JOIN characteristic c WITH (NOLOCK) ON qscl.char_id = c.char_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT scltg.char_id
					 FROM sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK)
					 INNER JOIN sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK) ON stg.sample_id = scltg.sample_id
					 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
					   AND stg.requested_time_utc >= @event_time_utc
					   AND (((stg.wo_id = @wo_id OR (stg.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
					   AND (stg.oper_id = @oper_id OR (stg.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
					   AND (stg.seq_no = @seq_no OR (stg.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL)))
					   OR (stg.wo_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.oper_id IS NOT NULL AND stg.seq_no IS NOT NULL AND @spec_priority = 11))
					   AND scltg.qm_spec_id <> @qm_spec_id
					 ) chars_accntd_by_other_specs ON c.char_id = chars_accntd_by_other_specs.char_id
		WHERE qscl.qm_spec_id = @qm_spec_id
			-- Exclude the characteristics whose severity code is set to 0 (UnUsed)
		  AND COALESCE(qscl.severity_cd, c.severity_cd) > 0
		  -- Retrieve all the characeristics that do not have a overidden plan_id OR
		  -- the characteristics that do have the overridden plan_id and the supplied plan_id match the plan_id of a characteristics.
		 AND ((qscl.plan_id = @plan_id) OR (qscl.plan_id IS NULL AND @plan_override = 0))
		 AND chars_accntd_by_other_specs.char_id IS NULL

	--Verify whether the spec has at least one characteristic to generate future samples.
	--If none, there is no point in looping through different times to see whether a sample need to be generated.
	--Do this for efficiency purpose.
	--Verify whether all the characteristics for this spec was already accounted. If so, exit.
	IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @chars_to_be_collected)
		RETURN

	--Default the sample request time to the current time
	--For shift frequency (0) when executed in the context of shift change, then the shift start time is the sample_start_time.
	SELECT @sample_start_time_utc = COALESCE(@sample_start_time_utc, @event_time_utc), @sample_counter = 1

	--Default the sample request time utc to sample start time utc as the first sample request time.
	SET @sample_requested_time_utc = @sample_start_time_utc

	IF (@freq_type = 0) BEGIN -- Shift
		-- Verify whether the offset end is specified, and if not, default the sample end time to the shift end time.
		-- Do not allow samples to be generated at the shift end time that would fall on the next shift.
		-- Therefore, reduce one second from the shift end time.
		IF (@offset_end_sec IS NULL) SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, -1, @shift_end_time_utc)
		-- If the offset end time is not null, then apply the offset end time to the end of the shift.
		ELSE SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, -@offset_end_sec, @shift_end_time_utc)
	END
	ELSE IF (@freq_type IN (1,2,3) ) BEGIN -- 1: Calendar, 2: Runtime, 3: Production
		-- Verify whether the offset end is specified, and if not, default the sample end time to the shift end time.
		-- Do not allow samples to be generated at the shift end time that would fall on the next shift.
		-- Therefore, reduce one second from the shift end time.
		IF (@offset_end_sec IS NULL) SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, -1, @shift_end_time_utc)
		--If the offset end time is not null, then apply the offset to the event time
		--representing the amount of time in the future to project samples.
		ELSE SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, @offset_end_sec, @event_time_utc)
		-- If we have a production frequency, check to see if the time to produce the
		-- remaining quantity is less than offset end or the end of the shift
		IF (@freq_type = 3 AND @prod_offset_end_sec IS NOT NULL) -- Production
		BEGIN
			IF (DATEADD(SS, @prod_offset_end_sec, @event_time_utc) < @sample_end_time_utc_offset)
			BEGIN
				SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, @prod_offset_end_sec, @event_time_utc)
			END
		END
	END
	-- Do not allow samples to be generated at the shift end time that would fall on the next shift.
	-- Therefore, reduce one second from the shift end time.
	ELSE SET @sample_end_time_utc_offset = DATEADD(SS, -1, @shift_end_time_utc)  -- Default to shift end time

	--Default the sample end time with offset as the end time of the samples.
	SET @sample_end_time_utc = @sample_end_time_utc_offset

	-- Verify whether the QM spec has an end effectivity date that is lower than the sample end time (UTC), and if yes,
	-- replace the sample end time with the end effectivity date from the QM spec.
	IF (@qm_spec_end_eff_utc IS NOT NULL AND @qm_spec_end_eff_utc < @sample_end_time_utc)
		--Since the QM spec ends earlier than the shift/or with offset, reset the last sample time with spec end effectivity time.
		SET @sample_end_time_utc = @qm_spec_end_eff_utc

	IF (@freq_type = 0 OR @freq_type = 3) BEGIN --Shift
		IF (@freq_type = 0 AND @offset_start_sec IS NOT NULL)
			--If the offset start time is not null, then apply the start offset to the start time of the shift.
			SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, @offset_start_sec, @sample_start_time_utc)

		--Verify whether sample interval and samples per shift are both null, and if yes, then generate one sample in a shift.
		IF (@sample_interval_sec IS NULL AND @samples_per_shift IS NULL) BEGIN -- both sample interval and samples per shift is null
				IF (@sample_requested_time_utc <= @sample_end_time_utc) -- Verify whether the sample request time is less than or equal to the sample end time.
					--Generate one sample for this shift.
					INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (requested_time_utc, char_id)
					SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc, c.char_id
					FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
		END

		--Verify whether any fixed number of samples to be created in a shift.
		ELSE IF (@sample_interval_sec IS NULL) BEGIN -- Fixed number of samples to be created in a shift.
			--This frequency requires a fixed number of samples to be created in a shift.
			--Therefore, calculate the time interval between samples such that the amount of time between samples are equal
			--The reason why the denominator contains @samples_per_shift-1 is that there are only n-1 interval between samples.
			--For example, let's say the shift time is between 4a - 8a, and if 5 samples are requested in a shift, then there
			--are only 4 intervals between each sample.  I.e., the first sample is at 4a and the last sample is at 07:59:59, and the
			--remaining samples are at 5a, 6a and 7a.  Thus, the intervals are 4-5, 5-6, 6-7 and 7-8.
			IF COALESCE(@samples_per_shift, 0) < 2 SET @samples_per_shift = 1
			ELSE IF (DATEADD(SS, 1, @sample_end_time_utc) = @shift_end_time_utc) SET @sample_interval_sec = DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @shift_end_time_utc)/(@samples_per_shift-1)
			ELSE SET @sample_interval_sec = DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @sample_end_time_utc_offset)/(@samples_per_shift-1)

			--Determine the next sample requested time UTC, if the current time is not the shift start time.
			IF (@sample_requested_time_utc < @event_time_utc) BEGIN
				--Determine how many samples are already accounted in the shift, so that those samples are not reaccounted.
				SET @sample_counter = CEILING(DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @event_time_utc)/@sample_interval_sec) + 1

				--The purpose of this statement and the previous statement is to eliminate the past samples in a shift, if the shift start was more than 5 minutes in the past from the shift start time for an entity.
				--The reason is that there may be a sample frequency with 30 seconds time interval between samples, and if the shift start happens in the middle of the shift, there is no reason to
				--go back in the past to generate all the samples, as they will be removed anyway before they are writeen into sample_*_go tables.
				SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, CEILING(DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @event_time_utc)/@sample_interval_sec)*@sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc)
			END

			--Loop through each time interval in a shift to create samples.
			WHILE (@sample_counter <= @samples_per_shift) BEGIN
				--If the current sample requested time is less than the sample end time utc, then create a sample
				IF (@sample_requested_time_utc <= @sample_end_time_utc)
					INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (requested_time_utc, char_id)
					SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc, c.char_id
					FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
				ELSE BREAK -- The current sample requested time is greater than the sample end time UTC.

				--If this is the last sample to be created in a shift and the sample requested time is the shift end time,
				--then generate a sample that is one second less than the shift end time.
				IF (@sample_counter = @samples_per_shift - 1 AND DATEADD(SS, 1, @sample_end_time_utc_offset) = @shift_end_time_utc) SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, -1, @shift_end_time_utc)
				--Add the interval to the current sample requested time.  If this is a production frequency, them
				--use the seconds in the first prod sample unless that is null in which case the seconds in the sample interval
				--should be used
				ELSE SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc)
				--Increment the counter by 1.
				SET @sample_counter = @sample_counter + 1
			END

		END -- Fixed number of samples to be created in a shift.

		ELSE BEGIN -- Samples ought to be generated based on the time interval, and handle no. of samples per shift if applicable.
			--Determine the next sample requested time UTC, if the current time is not the shift start time.
			IF (@sample_requested_time_utc < @event_time_utc) BEGIN
				--Determine how many samples are already accounted in the shift, so that those samples are not reaccounted.
				SET @sample_counter = CEILING(DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @event_time_utc)/@sample_interval_sec) + 1

				--The purpose of this statement and the previous statement is to eliminate the past samples in a shift, if the shift start was more than 5 minutes in the past from the shift start time for an entity.
				--The reason is that there may be a sample frequency with 30 seconds time interval between samples, and if the shift start happens in the middle of the shift, there is no reason to
				--go back in the past to generate all the samples, as they will be removed anyway before they are writeen into sample_*_go tables.
				SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, CEILING(DATEDIFF(SS, @sample_requested_time_utc, @event_time_utc)/@sample_interval_sec)*@sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc)
			END

			--Generate the sample till the sample requested time is less than the sample end time UTC.
			WHILE ((@sample_requested_time_utc <= @sample_end_time_utc)
				AND (@sample_counter <= COALESCE(@samples_per_shift, @sample_counter))) BEGIN
				INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (requested_time_utc, char_id)
				SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc, c.char_id
				FROM @chars_to_be_collected c

				--Increment the sample counter
				SET @sample_counter = @sample_counter + 1

				--Verify whether there are enough samples generated as per the number of samples per shift configuration.
				IF (@samples_per_shift IS NOT NULL AND @sample_counter > @samples_per_shift)
					--Exit if the number of samples are generated as per the samples per shift configuration.
					BREAK

				--Add the interval to the current sample requested time.  If this is a production frequency, them
				--use the seconds in the first prod sample unless that is null in which case the seconds in the sample interval
				--should be used
				SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, COALESCE(@first_prod_sample_sec, @sample_interval_sec), @sample_requested_time_utc)

				--Set the first production sample seconds to null so that the sample interval seconds is used for the
				-- remaining samples
				SET @first_prod_sample_sec = NULL
			END

		END -- Samples ought to be generated based on the time interval, and handle no. of samples per shift if applicable.
	END -- freq_type = 0 OR 3: Shift

	ELSE IF (@freq_type = 1) BEGIN -- Calendar time
		-- Determine the start and end times for the samples.
		--Verify whether the offset start is specified
		IF (@offset_start_sec IS NOT NULL) BEGIN -- There is offset start configured for this frequency, so the samples are generated for a fixed time in a day,
			-- regardless of when that characteristic was last collected.
			-- This frequency has offset start time configured.  Therefore, the start times and the end times are considered in entity's local time.
			-- Default the sample_start_time_local to midnight of this day or the sample_start_time_local to the midnight of this week.

			--Get the sample requested time in local.
			SELECT @sample_requested_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_utc)

			--Build samples for each characteristic for each time span.
			--Verify whether the sample request time falls within the sample end time boundary.
			WHILE (@sample_requested_time_utc <= @sample_end_time_utc) BEGIN

				--Reset the start time to the start of the DAY. I.e. 00:00:00.  For Example, Sunday 00:00:00, Monday 00:00:00, Tuesday 00:00:00, etc.
				SET @day_or_week_start = DATEADD(DD, 0, DATEDIFF(DD, 0, @sample_requested_time_local))

				IF (@interval_unit = 3 OR @interval_unit = 4) -- Reset the start time to the beginning of the WEEK. I.e. Sunday 00:00:00
					SET @day_or_week_start = DATEADD(DD, -DATEPART(WEEKDAY, @day_or_week_start)+1, @day_or_week_start)

				--Add the offset value to the start time.  For example, if this frequency has a start offset of 5 hours 45 minutes
				--with 1 hour interval between samples.  If this SP is called at 2012-01-23 02:00:00 (local time), then
				--the start time of the first sample is Monday 05:45:00.  I.e. the variable below is adjusted with the offset start time.
				--Hence, the variable @start_time_local_offset will have 2012-01-23 05:45:00.
				--However, the @day_or_week_start will have 2012-01-23 00:00:00.
				SET @start_time_local_offset = DATEADD(SS, @offset_start_sec, @day_or_week_start)

				--Verify whether the star_time_local_offset is less than the sample requested time.  If yes, then samples are requested
				--after the actual first sample of the day/week, therefore find out when is the next sample.  If no, then default the
				--first sample time is equivalent to the offset time.
				IF (@start_time_local_offset < @sample_requested_time_local)
					--The sample request time is beyond the offset time.  Using the example above, the sample request time must be
					--2012-01-23 06:00:00, 2012-01-23 07:00:00, etc. therefore find the next sample time.
					--If the sample request is at 2012-01-23 06:00:00, then the next sample is at 2012-01-23 06:45:00,
					--because the 2012-01-23 05:45:00 is before 2012-01-23 06:00:00.
					--Similarly, if the sample request is at 2012-01-23 07:00:00, then the next sample is at 2012-01-23 07:45:00
					SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(SS, CEILING(DATEDIFF(SS, @start_time_local_offset, @sample_requested_time_local)/@sample_interval_sec)*@sample_interval_sec, @start_time_local_offset)
				ELSE
					--The sample request time (or the current time) is not greater than the time to which the offset is applied.
					--Therefore, default the sample request time to the time for which the offset is applied.
					--In this case the sample request time is on or before  2012-01-23 05:45:00.  For example,  2012-01-23 02:00:00,  2012-01-23 03:00:00, etc.
					SET @sample_requested_time_local = @start_time_local_offset

				--Verify whether the modified sample request time is outside the day or week boundary.
				--If yes, then reset the sample request time to the beginning of the next day or beginning of the next week.
				IF ((@interval_unit IN (3,4) AND (@sample_requested_time_local >= DATEADD(WK, 1, @day_or_week_start))) -- Days or Week
					OR (@interval_unit IN (0,1,2) AND @sample_requested_time_local >= DATEADD(DD, 1, @day_or_week_start))) BEGIN -- Seconds, Minutes, Hours
						--Reset the sample requested time local to the beginning of the next day or beginning of the next week.
					IF (@interval_unit = 3 OR @interval_unit = 4) -- Days or Week
						--Since the modified local time falls on the next week, reset the sample requested time to the starting time of the next week.
						SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(WK, 1, @day_or_week_start)
					ELSE -- Seconds, Minutes, Hours
						--Since the modified local time falls on the next day, reset the sample requested time to the starting time of the next day.
						--From the previous example, adding 1 hour to the 2012-01-23 11:45:00 results 2012-01-24 00:45:00 (next day) from the if condition
						--"IF (@start_time_local_offset < @sample_requested_time_local)" - 1st part.  However, the offset for the day is 5 hours 45 minutes,
						--therefore, reset the sample requested time to the beginning of the next day 2012-01-24 00:00:00.
						SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(DD, 1, @day_or_week_start)

					--Get the sample requested time UTC using the sample requested time local.
					SET @sample_requested_time_utc = dbo.fn_TZ_GetUtcDateFromLocal(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_local, @sample_requested_time_utc)
				END -- The sample requested time is outside the day or week boundary.

				ELSE BEGIN -- The sample requested time is NOT outside the the day or week boundary.
					--Get the sample requested time in UTC.
					SET @sample_requested_time_utc = dbo.fn_TZ_GetUtcDateFromLocal(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_local, @sample_requested_time_utc)

					--Verify whether the sample requested time is less than the sample end time UTC
					--and the sample requested time is greater than the offset start time of the day or week.
					--If yes, then generate a future sample at this time.
					IF (@sample_requested_time_utc <= @sample_end_time_utc AND @sample_requested_time_local >= @start_time_local_offset) BEGIN
						INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (requested_time_utc, char_id)
						SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc, c.char_id
						FROM @chars_to_be_collected c

						-- Increment the sample counter
						SET @sample_counter = @sample_counter + 1
					END

					--If the interval unit is Seconds or Minutes or Hours, sample time increments are handled with UTC times;
					--otherwise, the sample time increments are handled in local times.
					IF (@interval_unit IN (0, 1, 2)) BEGIN -- Seconds, Minuts, Hours
						--If the interval unit is Seconds or Minutes or Hours, then handle the sample request time (incrementing the times) in terms of UTC.
						--The reason is that the UTC always moves forward and the local time is just a representation of a time in local.
						--For example, if samples are requested for every one hour from the start offset of 1 hour and the day is 2012-11-04 01:00:00,
						--then we may need a sample at 2012-11-04 01:00:00 (local) and 2012-11-04 05:00:00 (UTC)
						--and 2012-11-04 01:00:00 (local) and 2012-11-04 06:00:00 (UTC).
						--If the sample time increments are handled in local time, then there is no way to accommodate the 2012-11-04 01:00:00 (local) sample
						--for the 2012-11-04 06:00:00 (UTC), because adding 1 hour to the 2012-11-04 01:00:00 (local) results 2012-11-04 02:00:00 (local)
						--causing 2012-11-04 01:00:00 (local) and 2012-11-04 06:00:00 (UTC) to be missed.
						--Add the interval to the current sample request time.
						SET @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc)

						--Verify whether the new local time is greater than the previous local time + interval
						SELECT @next_sample_request_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_utc)
							, @curr_sample_request_time_local = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_local)
						--Verify whether the new local time is greater than the previous local time + interval
						IF  (@next_sample_request_time_local > @curr_sample_request_time_local
							AND DATEDIFF(D, @next_sample_request_time_local, @curr_sample_request_time_local) = 0) BEGIN
							--This is a special case, when the clock moves forward by 1 hour, but the local times do not have the same difference time.
							--For example, the interval is configured to have a sample every 90 minutes with the start offset of 90 minutes from the day.
							--On the day of the DST change (for example 2012-03-11, the clock moves from 2012-03-11 02:00:00 to 2012-03-11 03:00:00 - both local times),
							--there is no local time between 2012-03-11 02:00:00 and 2012-03-11 03:00:00.
							--Therefore, the first sample of the day is created at 2012-03-11 01:30:00 (local) and 2012-03-11 06:30:00 (UTC)
							--Now, when the UTC time is incremented by 90 minutes, it becomes 2012-03-11 08:00:00 (UTC) and 2012-03-11 04:00:00 (local).
							--Since 2012-03-11 04:00:00 (local) is greater than the previous time slot (2012-03-11 03:00:00), it resets the next sample to be
							--generated at 2012-03-11 04:30:00 causing the 03:00:00 sample to be missed.
							--To solve this problem, when the difference between the previous local time (2012-03-11 01:30:00) and
							--the next local time (2012-03-11 04:30:00) is greater than the sample interval time (>90 in this case) and
							--the difference in the day between the previous local time and the next local time is zero (i.e. same day),
							--then reset the local time to be the previous sample time (2012-03-11 01:30:00) + interval (90) = 2012-03-11 03:00:00
							SET @sample_requested_time_local = @curr_sample_request_time_local

							--Get the corresponding UTC time.
							SET @sample_requested_time_utc = dbo.fn_TZ_GetUtcDateFromLocal(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_local, @sample_requested_time_utc)
						END
						ELSE -- Continue with the normal flow.
							--Get the sample requested time in local.
							SET @sample_requested_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_utc)

					END -- Seconds, Minuts, Hours
					ELSE BEGIN -- Days or Weeks
						--One sample is requested in a day or in a week.  Therefore, handle the sample request times in local.
						--The reason is that handling the sample requested times in UTC may cause a sample to be missed when the
						--clock moves forward.
						--For example, if one sample is requested every day with a start offset of 1 hour, and the day is 2012-03-11 01:00:00
						--Then the first sample is at 2012-03-11 01:00:00 (local) and 2012-03-11 06:00:00 (UTC).
						--The next sample is at 2012-03-12 01:00:00 (local) and 2012-03-11 05:00:00 (UTC).
						--If the sample time increments are handled in UTC time, then adding 1 day to the 2012-03-11 06:00:00 (UTC)
						--results 2012-03-12 06:00:00 (UTC) and 2012-03-12 02:00:00 (local), which is greater than 2012-03-12 01:00:00 (local).
						--So, this SP assumes the requested time in local is past the offset start time of the day, so it increments the day by 1,
						--hence moving the sample request time to next day causing a sample on 2012-03-12 01:00:00 (local) to be missed.
						SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_local)

						--Get the UTC time using the sample requested time  local.
						SET @sample_requested_time_utc = dbo.fn_TZ_GetUtcDateFromLocal(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_local, @sample_requested_time_utc)
					END  -- Days or Weeks

					--Verify whether the modified sample request time is outside the day or week boundary.
					--If yes, then reset the sample request time to the beginning of the next day or beginning of the next week.
					IF ((@interval_unit IN (3,4) AND (@sample_requested_time_local >= DATEADD(WK, 1, @day_or_week_start))) -- Days or Weeks
						OR (@interval_unit IN (0,1,2) AND @sample_requested_time_local >= DATEADD(DD, 1, @day_or_week_start))) BEGIN -- Seconds or Minutes or Hours
							--Reset the sample requested time local to the beginning of the next day or beginning of the next week.
						IF (@interval_unit = 3 OR @interval_unit = 4) -- Days or Weeks
							--Since the modified local time falls on the next week, reset the sample requested time to the starting time of the next week.
							SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(WK, 1, @day_or_week_start)
						ELSE  -- Seconds, Minutes, Hours
							--Since the modified local time falls on the next day, reset the sample requested time to the starting time of the next day.
							--Using the example at the beginning of this while loop, adding 1 hour
							--to the 2012-01-23 11:45:00 results 2012-01-24 00:45:00 (next day). However, the offset for the day is 5 hours 45 minutes,
							--therefore, reset the sample requested time to the beginning of the next day 2012-01-24 00:00:00
							SET @sample_requested_time_local = DATEADD(DD, 1, @day_or_week_start)

						--Get the UTC time using the sample requested time  local.
						SET @sample_requested_time_utc = dbo.fn_TZ_GetUtcDateFromLocal(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_local, @sample_requested_time_utc)
					END -- Handling sample request times falls ouside the day or week boundary.
				END -- The sample requested time is outside the day or week boundary.

				-- Do not allow samples to be created for more than 5 shifts (8 hr) in the future with 30 seconds interval between samples
				IF (@sample_counter >= 4800) BREAK
			END

		END -- There is offset start configured for this frequency
		ELSE BEGIN -- There is no offset start configured for this frequency, therefore, default the start time as of now.
			-- Since there is no offset start configured for this frequency, the characteristics ought to be measured at a time
			-- that the difference between the requested time and the previous requested time for a characteristic must be at least
			-- greater than or equal to the interval configured for this frequency.
			INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (char_id, requested_time_utc, existing_sample)
			SELECT c.char_id, COALESCE(MAX(sample_char.requested_time_utc), @sample_requested_time_utc)
			, CASE WHEN MAX(sample_char.requested_time_utc) IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
			FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
			LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT c.char_id, MAX(requested_time_utc) requested_time_utc
							FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
							INNER JOIN sample_char_link scl WITH (NOLOCK) ON c.char_id = scl.char_id
							INNER JOIN sample s WITH (NOLOCK) ON scl.sample_id = s.sample_id
							LEFT OUTER JOIN sample_freq sf WITH (NOLOCK) ON s.freq_id = sf.freq_id
							WHERE s.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
							  AND s.requested_time_utc > DATEADD(SS, -@sample_interval_sec, @sample_start_time_utc)
							  AND s.requested_time_utc <= @sample_start_time_utc
							  --AND (s.item_id = @item_id OR (s.item_id IS NULL AND @item_id IS NULL))
							  AND (s.wo_id = @wo_id OR (s.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
							  AND (s.oper_id = @oper_id OR (s.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
							  AND (s.seq_no = @seq_no OR (s.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL))
							  AND NOT (s.freq_id IS NOT NULL AND sf.freq_type = 19)
							GROUP BY c.char_id
							UNION
							SELECT c.char_id, MAX(requested_time_utc) requested_time_utc
							FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
							INNER JOIN sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK) ON c.char_id = scltg.char_id
							INNER JOIN sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK) ON scltg.sample_id = stg.sample_id
							WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
							  AND stg.requested_time_utc > DATEADD(SS, -@sample_interval_sec, @sample_start_time_utc)
							  AND stg.requested_time_utc <= @sample_start_time_utc
							  --AND (stg.item_id = @item_id OR (stg.item_id IS NULL AND @item_id IS NULL))
							  AND (stg.wo_id = @wo_id OR (stg.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
							  AND (stg.oper_id = @oper_id OR (stg.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
							  AND (stg.seq_no = @seq_no OR (stg.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL))
							GROUP BY c.char_id) sample_char ON sample_char.char_id = c.char_id
			GROUP BY c.char_id

			--Build samples for each characteristic for each time span, but do not allow samples to be created for more than 5 shifts.
			--For example, let's say there is a sample generated for a characteristic using shift frequency at 12:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00
			--The time of triggering to generate samples is at 12:00p, and the calendar frequency is configured to generate samples every 45 minutes.
			--Therefore, the while block below checks for a sample at each time slot, i.e. 12:00, 12:45, 13:30, 14:15, 15:00, 15:45
			--At 12:00, the last sample was requested at 12:00
			--At 12:45, the last sample requested returns 12:00 (from the current temp table collection), and the query returning existing future samples checks whether
			--	there are any samples between 12:00 and 12:45, and if any then that sample is inserted into the temp table; otherwise the next sample (12:00 + 45 mins = 12:45) is returned.
			--At 13:30, the last sample requested returns 12:45 (from the current temp table collection), and the query returning existing future samples checks whether
			--  there are any samples between 12:45 and 13:30, and it finds there is a 13:00 sample created by shift frequency and that sample is less than the 13:30,
			--  therefore the sample at 13:00 is inserted in the temporary table collection.
			--At 14:15, the last sample requested returns 13:00. Since there are no samples between 13:00 and 13:45, the next sample is requested at 13:45.

			--Verify whether there are characteristics for which there are NO samples in the future.
			IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @chars_to_be_collected WHERE char_exists = 0) BEGIN

				SET @sample_counter = 1

				INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (char_id, requested_time_utc, existing_sample, first_sample_set)
				SELECT c.char_id, CASE WHEN LastSampleRequested.requested_time_utc IS NULL THEN @sample_requested_time_utc ELSE LastSampleRequested.requested_time_utc END, 0, 1
				FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
				LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT char_id, DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, MAX(requested_time_utc)) AS requested_time_utc
							 FROM @sample_characteristic
							 GROUP BY char_id
							) LastSampleRequested ON c.char_id = LastSampleRequested.char_id
				WHERE c.char_exists = 0

				--There are characteristics for which there are no samples in the future
				--Loop through each sample request time for these characteristics and generate samples in the future.
				WHILE (@sample_requested_time_utc <= DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_end_time_utc)) BEGIN

					INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (char_id, requested_time_utc, existing_sample, first_sample_set)
					--The next sample time is the last sample requested time for a characteristic plus the sample interval time
					SELECT LastSampleRequested.char_id, DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec*@sample_counter, LastSampleRequested.requested_time_utc), 0, 0
					FROM @sample_characteristic LastSampleRequested
					WHERE LastSampleRequested.first_sample_set = 1

					--Increment the sample set by 1.
					SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc), @sample_counter = COALESCE(@sample_counter, 1) + 1

					-- Do not allow samples to be created for more than 5 shifts (8 hr) in the future with 30 seconds interval between samples
					IF (@sample_counter >= 4800) BREAK
				END -- End the loop for creating samples in the future.
			END --Verify whether there are characteristics for which there are NO samples in the future.

			--Default the sample request time to the sample start time.
			SET @sample_requested_time_utc = @sample_start_time_utc

			--Verify whether there are characteristics for which there are samples exist in the future.
			IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @chars_to_be_collected WHERE char_exists = 1) BEGIN

				SET @sample_counter = 1

				WHILE (@sample_requested_time_utc <= DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_end_time_utc)) BEGIN

					;WITH cteLastSampleRequested (char_id, requested_time_utc)
					AS
						--Get the LAST sample requested time from the current collection for each characteristic.
						(SELECT LastSampleRequested.char_id, MAX(LastSampleRequested.requested_time_utc) AS requested_time_utc
						 FROM @sample_characteristic LastSampleRequested
						 INNER JOIN @chars_to_be_collected c ON LastSampleRequested.char_id = c.char_id
						 WHERE c.char_exists = 1
						 GROUP BY LastSampleRequested.char_id
						),
					cteExistingFutureSamples (char_id, requested_time_utc)
					AS
						--Get the NEXT requested time (if any) for each characteristic.
						(SELECT c.char_id, MAX(stg.requested_time_utc) requested_time_utc
						 FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
						 INNER JOIN sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK) ON c.char_id = scltg.char_id
						 INNER JOIN sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK) ON scltg.sample_id = stg.sample_id
						 LEFT OUTER JOIN cteLastSampleRequested last_char_requested ON scltg.char_id = last_char_requested.char_id
						 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
						   AND c.char_exists = 1
						   --Get the highest sample that occurs between the last sample and the interval time of the calendar frequency.
						   AND stg.requested_time_utc > last_char_requested.requested_time_utc
						   AND stg.requested_time_utc <= DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, last_char_requested.requested_time_utc)
						   --AND (stg.item_id = @item_id OR (stg.item_id IS NULL AND @item_id IS NULL))
						   AND (stg.wo_id = @wo_id OR (stg.wo_id IS NULL AND @wo_id IS NULL))
						   AND (stg.oper_id = @oper_id OR (stg.oper_id IS NULL AND @oper_id IS NULL))
						   AND (stg.seq_no = @seq_no OR (stg.seq_no IS NULL AND @seq_no IS NULL))
						 GROUP BY c.char_id
						)
					INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (char_id, requested_time_utc, existing_sample)
					SELECT c.char_id
						--If there is a sample requested for this characteristic and if that sample is less than the next sample request time, then use the existing sample time.
						,COALESCE(CASE WHEN exist_fut_sampls.requested_time_utc IS NOT NULL AND exist_fut_sampls.requested_time_utc <= DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, last_sampl_reqstd.requested_time_utc)
								 THEN exist_fut_sampls.requested_time_utc ELSE DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, last_sampl_reqstd.requested_time_utc) END, @sample_requested_time_utc)
						,CASE WHEN exist_fut_sampls.requested_time_utc IS NOT NULL AND exist_fut_sampls.requested_time_utc <= DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, last_sampl_reqstd.requested_time_utc)
								 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
					FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
					LEFT OUTER JOIN cteLastSampleRequested last_sampl_reqstd ON last_sampl_reqstd.char_id = c.char_id
					LEFT OUTER JOIN cteExistingFutureSamples exist_fut_sampls ON exist_fut_sampls.char_id = c.char_id
					WHERE c.char_exists = 1

					--Increment the sample set by 1.
					SELECT @sample_requested_time_utc = DATEADD(SS, @sample_interval_sec, @sample_requested_time_utc), @sample_counter = COALESCE(@sample_counter, 1) + 1

					-- Do not allow samples to be created for more than 5 shifts (8 hr) in the future with 30 seconds interval between samples
					IF (@sample_counter >= 4800) BREAK
				END
			END --Verify whether there are characteristics for which there are samples exist in the future.

			-- Remove all existing samples that are generated by other frequencies.
			DELETE FROM @sample_characteristic WHERE existing_sample = 1
		END -- There is no offset start configured for this frequency
	END -- freq_type = 1: Calendar time

	ELSE IF (@freq_type IN (6, 8, 20)) BEGIN -- 6: if production lot change, 8: if job start, 20: if job end
	    --Generate one sample for the production lot change, job start or job end event.
	    INSERT INTO @sample_characteristic (requested_time_utc, char_id)
	    SELECT @event_time_utc, c.char_id
	    FROM @chars_to_be_collected c
	END -- 6: if production lot change, 8: if job start, 20: if job end

	--Exit, if a frequency is not handled.
	ELSE RETURN

	-- Remove all the samples that are requested older than the supplied event time UTC (job start time or utilization reason change time, etc.)
	-- Probably there may be one sample for each characteristic as a starting sample to generate future samples for each characteristic and,
	-- the samples that are generated beyond the sample end time UTC ought to be removed (may be 1 or 2).
	DELETE FROM @sample_characteristic
	WHERE requested_time_utc < @sample_start_time_utc OR requested_time_utc < @event_time_utc
	   OR requested_time_utc > @sample_end_time_utc

	--Get the samples that do not exist in the database for a given time and the context.
	IF (@wo_id IS NULL)
		INSERT INTO @unique_future_samples (requested_time_utc, sample_name, sample_id, existing_sample)
		SELECT DISTINCT sc.requested_time_utc, existing_samples.sample_name, existing_samples.sample_id
			, CASE WHEN existing_samples.sample_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
		FROM @sample_characteristic sc
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT stg.requested_time_utc, stg.sample_name, stg.sample_id
						 FROM sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK)
						 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
						   AND stg.wo_id IS NULL AND stg.oper_id IS NULL AND stg.seq_no IS NULL
						   AND stg.plan_id = @plan_id) existing_samples ON existing_samples.requested_time_utc = sc.requested_time_utc
		ORDER BY sc.requested_time_utc
	ELSE
		INSERT INTO @unique_future_samples (requested_time_utc, sample_name, sample_id, existing_sample)
		SELECT DISTINCT sc.requested_time_utc, existing_samples.sample_name, existing_samples.sample_id
			, CASE WHEN existing_samples.sample_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
		FROM @sample_characteristic sc
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT stg.requested_time_utc, stg.sample_name, stg.sample_id
						 FROM sample_to_go stg WITH (NOLOCK)
						 WHERE stg.ent_id = @qm_ent_id
						   AND stg.wo_id = @wo_id AND stg.oper_id = @oper_id AND stg.seq_no = @seq_no
						   AND stg.plan_id = @plan_id) existing_samples ON existing_samples.requested_time_utc = sc.requested_time_utc
		ORDER BY sc.requested_time_utc

	--Default the boolean variable to false
	SET @templ_name_cont_char_name = CHARINDEX('[CHARACTERISTICNAME]', @sample_name_template, 0)
	--For the first sample, we want to check to see if there is a qm_context and qm_context_link
	IF (@freq_type = 3)
	BEGIN
		EXECUTE sp_S_QM_Context_GetContext @qm_ent_id, @wo_id, @oper_id, @seq_no, @context_ent_id, @context_item_id, @item_category_id, @context_oper_id, @process_id, @context_id OUTPUT
		IF (NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM qm_context_link  WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE context_id = @context_id AND freq_id = @freq_id))
			EXECUTE sp_i_QM_CONTEXT_LINK @context_id, @freq_id, 0, NULL, @item_id, 0, 0, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL

        -- For samples generated from a production count frequency, the item ID should always be written to the sample_to_go table
        -- even if the item is not part of the QM Specifications context.
		SET @context_item_id = COALESCE(@context_item_id, @item_id)

		-- If we are readying a sample, set the spare4 value to 1 as a flag to indicate
		-- that the sample should be readied.
		IF (@ready_prod_count_sample = 1) SET @spare4_value = '1'
	END

	DECLARE unique_samples_cursor CURSOR READ_ONLY FAST_FORWARD FOR
	SELECT requested_time_utc FROM @unique_future_samples WHERE existing_sample = 0 ORDER BY requested_time_utc

	OPEN unique_samples_cursor
	WHILE (1=1) BEGIN
		FETCH NEXT FROM unique_samples_cursor INTO @sample_requested_time_utc

		IF (@@FETCH_STATUS <> 0) BREAK

		SELECT @sample_requested_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @sample_requested_time_utc), @current_sample_no = NULL

		-- Get the first characteristic name ONLY if the sample name template contains the characteristic.
		IF @templ_name_cont_char_name > 0
			SELECT @char_name = c.char_name
			FROM characteristic c WITH (NOLOCK)
			WHERE c.char_id = (SELECT TOP 1 char_id FROM @sample_characteristic WHERE requested_time_utc = @sample_requested_time_utc)

		-- Get the sample name for this requested time
		EXEC sp_SA_GetNextSampleName @plan_id = @plan_id, @plan_name = @plan_name, @temp_sample_name = @sample_name_template, @reset_option = @reset_option
				, @requested_time_local = @sample_requested_time_local, @ent_name = @ent_name
				, @wo_id = @wo_id, @oper_id = @oper_id, @seq_no = @seq_no, @segment_requirement_id = NULL
				, @segment_response_id = NULL, @item_id = @item_id, @char_name = @char_name
				, @qm_spec_name = @qm_spec_name, @freq_name = @freq_name
				, @prev_sample_name_template = @sample_name_template, @prev_sample_name_instance = @prev_sample_name_instance, @prev_sample_no = @prev_sample_no
				, @next_sample_name = @sample_name OUTPUT, @sample_name_instance = @sample_name_instance OUTPUT
				, @next_sample_id = @current_sample_no OUTPUT

		--If the sample instance name is empty, then there are no replaceable parameters except octothorpes, therefore replace the instance name with '-'
		IF (@sample_name_instance = '') AND (@current_sample_no IS NOT NULL AND @current_sample_no > 0) SET @sample_name_instance = '-'

		--Copy the sample_name instance and current sample no to the previous sample name instance and number
		SELECT @prev_sample_name_instance = @sample_name_instance, @prev_sample_no = @current_sample_no

		SELECT @warning_time_utc = DATEADD(MI, @warning_interval_min, @sample_requested_time_utc), @expiry_time_utc = DATEADD(MI, @expiry_interval_min, @sample_requested_time_utc)

		--Create a sample to go record ONLY if the future sample identifying the unique key does not exist at this requested time.
		INSERT INTO sample_to_go (ent_id, sample_name, wo_id, oper_id, seq_no, context_ent_id
			, item_id, item_category_id, process_id, context_oper_id
			, freq_id, plan_id
			, requested_time_utc, requested_time_local
			, expiry_time_utc, expiry_time_local
			, warning_time_utc, warning_time_local
			, sample_name_template, sample_name_instance, current_sample_no, spare4
			, last_edit_by, last_edit_at)
		VALUES (@qm_ent_id, @sample_name, @wo_id, @oper_id, @seq_no, @context_ent_id
			, @context_item_id, @item_category_id, @process_id, @context_oper_id
			, @freq_id, @plan_id
			, @sample_requested_time_utc, @sample_requested_time_local
			, @expiry_time_utc, dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @expiry_time_utc)
			, @warning_time_utc, dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(@qm_ent_id, @warning_time_utc)
			, @sample_name_template, @sample_name_instance, @current_sample_no, @spare4_value
			, @user_id, @event_time_utc)

		SET @sample_id = SCOPE_IDENTITY()

		-- If we are generating a ready sample, clear the the spare4 value and
		-- the flag indicating that we are generating a ready sample
		IF (@ready_prod_count_sample = 1)
		BEGIN
			-- note that we readied a sample so we can ready sample char link records
			SET @spare4_value = null
			-- After we ready one sample, we want to turn off readying samples
			SET @ready_prod_count_sample = 0
		END

		--The purpose of updating the temporary table with the sample name is to uniquely identify the future sample in the sample_to_go table.
		INSERT INTO @unique_future_samples (requested_time_utc, sample_name, sample_id, existing_sample)
		VALUES (@sample_requested_time_utc, @sample_name, @sample_id, 1)
	END
	CLOSE unique_samples_cursor
	DEALLOCATE unique_samples_cursor

	--Remove any future samples that are left over.
	DELETE @unique_future_samples WHERE existing_sample = 0

	--Generate sample_char_link_to_go records using the identified sample requested times.
	--The reason for having a DISTINCT clause in the SELECT statement is that when the clock moves forward by 1 hour during DST change,
	--i.e. from 2012-03-11 02:00:00 to 2012-03-11 03:00:00, there is no local time between 2a and 3a.
	--So, when the clock moved from 2a to 3a, the SP thinks that a sample during that local time was missed.
	--Hence it adds a duplicate sample during this clock movement causing a primary key violation from the sample_char_link_to_go.
	--To avoid the primary key violation, the DISTINCT clause removes that duplicate sample name generated between 2a and 3a.
	--Case: Calendar frequency of 1 hour between samples with start offset of 15 minutes and end offset of 9 hours, Event Date Time: 2011-03-13 03:00:00 (UTC or 6a PST as in the DFS)
	INSERT INTO sample_char_link_to_go (sample_id, char_id, qm_spec_id, last_edit_by, last_edit_at)
	SELECT DISTINCT unique_future_samples.sample_id, sample_char.char_id, @qm_spec_id, @user_id, @event_time_utc
	FROM @sample_characteristic sample_char
	INNER JOIN @unique_future_samples unique_future_samples ON sample_char.requested_time_utc = unique_future_samples.requested_time_utc
	LEFT OUTER JOIN sample_char_link_to_go scltg WITH (NOLOCK) ON scltg.sample_id = unique_future_samples.sample_id AND scltg.char_id = sample_char.char_id
	WHERE scltg.char_id IS NULL
END

CREATE VIEW [dbo].[vw_group_production_data]
AS
SELECT item_prod.wo_id,
       item_prod.oper_id,
       item_prod.seq_no,
       job.act_start_time_utc,
       job.act_start_time_local,
       job.act_finish_time_utc,
       job.act_finish_time_local,
       job.qty_reqd,
       item_prod.shift_start_utc,
       item_prod.shift_start_local,
       item_prod.item_id,
       item.item_desc,
       item.num_decimals,
       uom.abbreviation units,
       item.item_class_id,
       item_class.item_class_desc,
       item_prod.lot_no,
       item_prod.sublot_no,
       item_prod.reas_cd,
       ireas.reas_desc,
       ireas.reas_grp_id,
       item_reas_grp.reas_grp_desc,
       item_prod.user_id,
       user_name.user_desc,
       item_prod.ent_id,
       ent.ent_name,
       ent_link.parent_ent_id,
       parent_ent.ent_name parent_ent_name,
       item_prod.shift_id,shift.shift_desc,
       item_prod.grade_cd,
       item_grade.item_grade_desc,
       item_grade.color grade_color,
       item_prod.status_cd,
       item_state.item_status_desc,
       item_state.color status_color,
       item_prod.to_ent_id,
       to_ent.ent_name to_ent_name,
       item_prod.good_prod,
       item_prod.qty_prod,
       item_prod.processed_flag,
       item_prod.byproduct,
       item_prod.move_status,
       item_prod.spare1,
       item_prod.spare2,
       item_prod.spare3,
       item_prod.spare4
FROM item_prod item_prod
INNER JOIN job job ON item_prod.wo_id = job.wo_id AND
                      item_prod.oper_id = job.oper_id AND
                      item_prod.seq_no = job.seq_no
INNER JOIN item item ON item_prod.item_id = item.item_id
INNER JOIN item_reas ireas ON
   item_prod.reas_cd = ireas.reas_cd
INNER JOIN user_name user_name ON
   item_prod.user_id = user_name.user_id
INNER JOIN ent ent ON item_prod.ent_id = ent.ent_id
INNER JOIN ent_link ent_link ON
   item_prod.ent_id = ent_link.child_ent_id
INNER JOIN shift shift ON
   item_prod.shift_id = shift.shift_id
INNER JOIN item_grade item_grade ON
   item_prod.grade_cd = item_grade.item_grade_cd
INNER JOIN item_state item_state ON
   item_prod.status_cd = item_state.item_status_cd
LEFT OUTER JOIN ent to_ent ON
   item_prod.to_ent_id = to_ent.ent_id
INNER JOIN uom uom ON item.uom_id = uom.uom_id
INNER JOIN item_class item_class ON
   item.item_class_id = item_class.item_class_id
INNER JOIN item_reas_grp item_reas_grp ON
   ireas.reas_grp_id = item_reas_grp.reas_grp_id
INNER JOIN ent parent_ent ON
   ent_link.parent_ent_id = parent_ent.ent_id

CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_SA_Storage_Exec_GetShrtages]
(@ent_id	INT	= NULL
) AS
--- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name	  - sp_SA_Storage_Exec_GetShrtages
-- Description	  - HD# 4890 Return a recordset resulting all items that are shortage along with shortage amount and reorder amount for each item
-- Author	      - Raghu
-- Date Created	  - 08/03/2004
-- Version	      - 6.2.0.0
--
-- Copyright (c) 2020 AVEVA Group plc and its subsidiaries. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Date_Modified  Modified_By	Ver	 Changes
-- 02/03/2005	  Raghu			2.1.13 Shortage Amount does not show up due to NULL value if a job does not run on an entity
-- 04/10/2007     Hari          3.2.06 HD#9618; To show 0 Qty Item (record in inventory) Shortages window
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- *************************************************************************************************************************
BEGIN
SET NOCOUNT ON


DECLARE  @process_level		INT
	,@child_level		INT

DECLARE @inv_temp TABLE(item_id NVARCHAR(40), item_desc NVARCHAR(80), min_inv_level FLOAT, shortage_amt FLOAT,
		 reorder_amt FLOAT, reorder_amt_max FLOAT)
DECLARE @ent_ids TABLE(ent_id int, ent_name varchar(80), description varchar(80), child_level INT)
DECLARE @ipl_temp TABLE (item_id NVARCHAR(40), item_desc NVARCHAR(80), process_id NVARCHAR(40), min_inv_level FLOAT,
		shortage_amt FLOAT, reorder_amt FLOAT, item_pref INT, last_edit_at DATETIME)

	--Find the shortages
	--check for item.min_inv_level > shortage_inv.shortage_amt
	INSERT INTO @inv_temp (item_id, item_desc, min_inv_level, shortage_amt, reorder_amt, reorder_amt_max)
	SELECT item.item_id, item.item_desc, item.min_inv_level, item.min_inv_level - ISNULL(shortage_inv.shortage_amt, 0) shortage_amt,
		item.reorder_amt, item.reorder_amt reorder_amt_max
	FROM item item LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT item_id, SUM(qty_left) shortage_amt FROM item_inv GROUP BY item_id) shortage_inv
		ON item.item_id = shortage_inv.item_id
	WHERE item.auto_reorder = 0 AND item.min_inv_level > 0 AND item.reorder_amt > 0
	UNION ALL
	SELECT isel.item_id, item.item_desc,isel.min_inv_level, isel.min_inv_level - ISNULL(shortage_inv.shortage_amt, 0) shortage_amt,
		isel.min_reorder_amt reorder_amt, isel_max.reorder_amt_max
	FROM item_storage_exec_link isel INNER JOIN item item ON item.item_id = isel.item_id
		INNER JOIN (SELECT item_id, MAX(min_reorder_amt) reorder_amt_max FROM item_storage_exec_link GROUP BY item_id) isel_max ON isel.item_id = isel_max.item_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT ent_id, item_id, SUM(qty_left) shortage_amt FROM item_inv GROUP BY ent_id, item_id)  shortage_inv
			ON isel.ent_id = shortage_inv.ent_id AND isel.item_id = shortage_inv.item_id
	WHERE item.auto_reorder = 0 AND item.min_inv_level > 0 AND item.reorder_amt > 0

	--If ent_id is not supplied
	IF (@ent_id IS NULL)
		SELECT DISTINCT inv_temp.item_id, inv_temp.item_desc, NULL 'process_id', MAX(inv_temp.min_inv_level) min_inv_level
			,MAX(inv_temp.shortage_amt) - ISNULL(MAX(wip_qty.qty_prod), 0) shortage_amt
			,MAX(inv_temp.reorder_amt_max) reorder_amt
		FROM @inv_temp inv_temp
		LEFT OUTER JOIN
			(SELECT j.item_id, SUM((ISNULL(j.qty_at_start, 0) - j.qty_prod)) qty_prod FROM job j WITH (NOLOCK)
			WHERE j.final_job = 1
			GROUP BY j.item_id) wip_qty
		ON inv_temp.item_id = wip_qty.item_id
		WHERE shortage_amt > (SELECT MAX(shortage_amt) -1 FROM @inv_temp WHERE item_id = inv_temp.item_id)
		  AND (inv_temp.shortage_amt - ISNULL(wip_qty.qty_prod, 0)) > 0
		GROUP BY inv_temp.item_id, inv_temp.item_desc
	ELSE BEGIN
		--If ent_id is supplied, filter items by those process_id with a level permitting it to be instantiated
		SELECT @process_level = CONVERT(INT, attr_value) FROM system_attr WHERE attr_id = 201
		SET @child_level = 1

		--Build the supplied entity and its ancestors into a temp table named @ent_ids
		INSERT INTO @ent_ids SELECT e.ent_id, e.ent_name, e.description, @child_level FROM ent e WHERE e.ent_id = @ent_id
		SET @child_level = 2

		WHILE (1=1) BEGIN
			INSERT INTO @ent_ids
				SELECT e.ent_id, e.ent_name, e.description, @child_level
				FROM ent_link el WITH (NOLOCK) INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON el.parent_ent_id = e.ent_id
				WHERE  el.child_ent_id IN (SELECT ent_id FROM @ent_ids WHERE child_level = @child_level -1)
			IF (@@ROWCOUNT <= 0) BREAK
			SET @child_level = @child_level + 1
		END

		INSERT INTO @ipl_temp (item_id, item_desc, process_id, min_inv_level, shortage_amt,
				reorder_amt, item_pref, last_edit_at)
		SELECT DISTINCT item_process.item_id, inv_temp.item_desc, item_process.process_id,
			MAX(inv_temp.min_inv_level) min_inv_level,
			MAX(inv_temp.shortage_amt) - ISNULL(MAX(wip_qty.qty_prod), 0) shortage_amt,
			MAX(inv_temp.reorder_amt_max) reorder_amt,
			MIN(ipl.item_pref) item_pref, MAX(ipl.last_edit_at) last_edit_at
		FROM @inv_temp inv_temp
		INNER JOIN
			(SELECT item_process_link.process_id, item_process_link.item_id, item.item_desc
			FROM item_process_link item_process_link WITH (NOLOCK)
			INNER JOIN item item WITH (NOLOCK) ON item_process_link.item_id = item.item_id
--			INNER JOIN process process WITH (NOLOCK) ON item_process_link.process_id = process.process_id
--			WHERE process.process_level >= @process_level
			WHERE item_process_link.status >= @process_level
			UNION
			SELECT bom_item_oper_link.process_id, bom_item_oper_link.parent_item_id, item.item_desc
			FROM bom_item_oper_link bom_item_oper_link WITH (NOLOCK)
			INNER JOIN item item WITH (NOLOCK) ON bom_item_oper_link.parent_item_id = item.item_id
--			INNER JOIN process process WITH (NOLOCK) ON bom_item_oper_link.process_id = process.process_id
			INNER JOIN item_process_link ipl WITH (NOLOCK) ON bom_item_oper_link.process_id = ipl.process_id AND bom_item_oper_link.parent_item_id = ipl.item_id
--			WHERE (bom_item_oper_link.bom_pos = 0) AND (process.process_level >= @process_level)) item_process
			WHERE (bom_item_oper_link.bom_pos = 0) AND (ipl.status >= @process_level)) item_process
		ON item_process.item_id = inv_temp.item_id
		INNER JOIN
			(SELECT oel.process_id FROM oper_ent_link oel WITH (NOLOCK)
			INNER JOIN oper oper WITH (NOLOCK) ON oel.process_id = oper.process_id AND oel.oper_id = oper.oper_id
--			INNER JOIN process p WITH (NOLOCK) ON oper.process_id = p.process_id
			WHERE oper.first_oper = 1 --AND p.process_status >= @process_level
			  AND oel.ent_id IN (SELECT ent_id FROM @ent_ids)) oelp
		ON item_process.process_id = oelp.process_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN
			(SELECT item_id, SUM((ISNULL(j.qty_at_start, 0) - j.qty_prod)) qty_prod FROM job j WITH (NOLOCK)
			WHERE final_job = 1
			GROUP BY j.item_id) wip_qty
		ON inv_temp.item_id = wip_qty.item_id
		INNER JOIN item_process_link ipl WITH (NOLOCK) ON item_process.item_id = ipl.item_id AND item_process.process_id = ipl.process_id
		WHERE shortage_amt > (SELECT MAX(shortage_amt) -1 FROM @inv_temp WHERE item_id = inv_temp.item_id)
		  AND (inv_temp.shortage_amt - ISNULL(wip_qty.qty_prod, 0)) > 0
		GROUP BY item_process.process_id, item_process.item_id, inv_temp.item_desc

		--From a list of items and processes, select a preferred process for an item where the item_pref
		--is the lowest preference level. If multiple processes results as the same lowest preference level,
		--then select the process which is last modified (instead of selecting any one process, get the latest process)
		SELECT  ipl_temp.item_id
			, ipl_temp.item_desc
			, ipl_temp.process_id
			, ipl_temp.min_inv_level
			, ipl_temp.shortage_amt
			, ipl_temp.reorder_amt
		FROM @ipl_temp ipl_temp
		WHERE process_id = (SELECT TOP 1 process_id FROM @ipl_temp
				WHERE item_id = ipl_temp.item_id
				  AND item_pref = (SELECT MIN(item_pref) FROM @ipl_temp WHERE item_id = ipl_temp.item_id)
				  AND last_edit_at = (SELECT MAX(last_edit_at) FROM @ipl_temp
							WHERE item_id = ipl_temp.item_id AND item_pref = ipl_temp.item_pref))
	END
END
