CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_SA_Line_GetBottleneckEnts]
(@line_id		INT32
,@log_prod_rates	BIT = 0
,@start_time_utc	TDATETIME = NULL
,@last_edit_comment	STRING254 = NULL
) AS
-- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name		- sp_SA_Line_GetBottleneckEnts
-- Description		- Returns a list of bottleneck entities
--                    UserStory: 178630 overrides Userstory: 149260
--						The nominal performance rate for a line is the expected production rate associated with the bottleneck entity/entities for that line.  The bottleneck entity is the enabled entity
--						with the lowest normalized production rate in the line, that is allowed to be a bottleneck.  If such entities at different child_order positions have the same rate, the one closest
--						to the end of the line is chosen as the bottleneck, though this does not directly affect the performance rate for the line.   In the case of parallel entities in a single
--						child_order position (column) the production rate is the normalized sum of the production rates for all of the entities at that child_order position that are enabled
--						(and if that child_order position is allowed to be a bottleneck � note that a line cannot be saved if some but not all entities at a child_order position can be part of the bottleneck).
--					    If that is lower than the production rate of the other child_order positions in the line, then all the enabled entities at that child_order position that are enabled and can be bottlenecks
--						are treated as the bottleneck.  In the case of parallel line segments spanning multiple child_order positions, the production rate for each child_order position is handled just as for the
--						bottleneck entities.  If the normalized sum of the production rates for all of the entities at that child_order position that are enabled and can be a bottleneck is lower than the
--						production rate of the other child_order positions in the line, then all the enabled entities at that child_order position that are enabled are treated as the bottleneck (
--						again, if that child_order position is allowed to be a bottleneck).

--						The expected production rate for a given entity is primarily the est_prod_rate field of the job record for the job running on the entity.  In order to compare this rate to other rates,
--						this number has to be converted into comparable units along with all the other production rates for a line.  This involves the prod_uom, batch size, and item_id fields. The est_prod_rate c
--						an be expressed as hours, minutes, or seconds per batch, or batches per hour, minute, or second.  This is what the prod_uom field defines.  The batch size is found in the batch_size field,
--						and the item to which the rate applies is found in the item_id field.  Clearly it would not do to say that a machne running at 20 batches per minute, where the batch size is 5
--						and the item is a 64 ounce bottle is running slower than a machine making 30 batches of 20 ounce bottles per hour with a batch size of 2.  The first 2 of these factors can be handled by
--						converting all rates to common prod_uom and batch_size values found in the fields of the same name in the line table.  The item conversion involved is a little harder � the native UOM of the item
--						is used to convert to the native UOM of another item.  In the case of coverting a 64 oz. bottle to a 20 oz. bottle (which should ordinarily be different item IDs), the native UOM of each will need
--						to be different, not a common value like "each" or "bottles", but rather "64 oz. bottle and "20 oz. bottle", with the conversion factor from the former to the latter being 3.2, assuming the
--						contents of the bottles is similar enough for the purpose of calculating comparable production rates (if not, item-specific conversions will need to be used, which the UOM_conv table accommodates).
--						Moreover, unlike prod_uom and batch_size, where it is possible to decide on a common prod_uom and batch size ahead of time and be guaranteed of being able to convert to those values,
--						it may not be possible to decide on a standard item to which all other things that are produced on a line may be converted.  If a standard item for the line is defined, then this
--						implicitly assumes that conversion is possible for all such items, and it should be used as the item to which all production rates for the individual entities are converted.

--						If an entity is not running any jobs, the next job that will be running on it is used.  This is not determined by the queue order of jobs scheduled to the entity, as this may not be set up
--						properly for entities in a line.  Rather it is gotten from the next upstream work order on the line, that has a job that will be done on the entity not currently running jobs
--						(which all upstream work orders should ordinarily have).  When looking upstream to find the next work order that will be done on this entity, the immediately preceding child_order position
--						is considered first, and if no jobs aere running there either, then the child_order position immediately before that one is considered.  If this process continues till the very beginning of the
--						line is reached, and no jobs are running there either, then the default production rate for the entity (from the oee_exec table) is used.  (The queue of work orders for the line is not
--						checked for the next job that is expected to be started on the line.)  If the entity not running any jobs is in a line segment and is not first, the entities in the preceding
--						child_order positions are restricted to those in the same line segment, until the first entity in the line segment is reached.  If the search for the next upstream work order finds multiple
--						work orders at a child_order position, the one that ought to get done first is used.

--						In the case of an entity shared between/among multiple production lines, only jobs for work orders being run on the production line for which the performance rate is to be gotten are considered;
--						other jobs, whether being run on the shared entity, or upstream of it on a different production line, are ignored.  The first test of whether a job is to be considered for a shared entity in the
--						context of a particular production line is whether that job's work order is queued to the line of interest or to one of the other lines with which the entity is shared.  If neither, then the queues
--						of the first non-shared entities preceding the entity under consideration or, if there are none, the first non-shared entities following the entity under consideration need to be searched for jobs
--						with the same work order.  In the case of preceding entities, allowance must be made for the possibility that the job is finished (but is still identified to the entity and having been run on it,
--						via the job's run_ent_id field).  Finished jobs should only be considered if a job for the same work order cannot be found in the preceding entities' queues with a less-than-complete state.
--						The job is deemed to belong to whichever line the entity belongs that has a job of the same work order in its queue.  (If qualifying jobs for the same work order are found in the queues of
--						entities belonging to different lines, then the line for the job on the shared entity under consideration cannot be determined, and an error should be returned.

-- Author			- Raghu G
-- Date Created		- 03/07/2013
-- Version			- 4.6
--
-- Copyright (c) 2020 AVEVA Group plc and its subsidiaries. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Change Date	Change By	Ver.	Changes
-- 05/21/2013	Raghu		4.6	Userstory: 178630
-- 06/18/2013	Raghu		4.6	Userstory: 196762: As Bruce, I need existing functionality to be retrofitted to detect a disabled entity on a line based on a specific utilization reason
-- 07/15/2013	Raghu		4.6	Userstory: 208003: As Bruce, I want the Production Rate and Bottleneck History table populated when the production rate and bottleneck entities change so I can use the data to calculate various KPIs
-- 08/14/2014	Raghu		4.6	UserStory: 226242: As Bruce, I want to indicate that a specific line position "IS" the bottleneck.
-- 09/18/2013	Raghu		4.6	UserStory: 238943: As Bruce, I want the preformance rate of the entity that is the bottleneck to be returned.
-- 10/09/2013	Raghu		4.6	UserStory: 245860: As Bruce, I want the highest priority utilization reason to be returned for the bottleneck entity in the line.
-- 09/08/2014	Raghu		5.0	UserStory: 390858: As Michelle, I want to know the reason why the bottleneck rate cannot be accurately calculated to determine the status of a line.
-- 08/15/2019   Raghu		6.2	UserStory: 1214549 - MOL: As AVEVA, I want to fix CR L00154675 (part 2 of HF CR L00150964: Line Monitor page doesn't show the correct utilization details) so that line monitor correctly shows bottleneck information
-- 09/17/2019	Raghu		6.2	UserStory: 1218531 - MOL:  As AVEVA, I want to fix CR L00154675 so I can obtain bottleneck summary information for lines having multiple positions where only one is set to "can be bottleneck"
-- 20/11/2019   Srinivasa   6.2 UserStory: 1227593 MOL: As Aveva, I want to merge L00155162 (HF CR L00154526: SR 103160978 An issue with the UOM not converting for an Item in the Web portal when going from one entity to another and the portal is showing an error that UOM doesn't exist.)
-- 05/21/2020	Raghu G		6.2	US-1312889-As AVEVA, I want to fix CR L00151312 so that the Line KPI calculations use the job's prod rate and not the entity default rate (Part 2)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--Context 1: Refers to missing line configuration
--Context 2: Refers to missing configuration for the entity/job configuration, such no conversion factors between two different UOMs, no default std_item_id for the entity, etc.
--Context 3: Refers to misconfiguration - can_be_bottleneck is set to false, but the entity is identified as bottleneck, the current utilization reason for an entity disables the entity, etc.
--Context 4: Bottleneck entity and rate are identified, but a line status cannot be determined due to the fact that there is no current utilization reason for the bottleneck entity.

SET NOCOUNT ON
SET XACT_ABORT ON

DECLARE @line_route TABLE(column_position INT, prev_column_position INT, col_pos_row_num INT, ent_id INT, child_order INT
							, segment_no INT, can_be_bottleneck BIT)

DECLARE	@production_rates	TABLE(column_position INT, child_order INT, ent_id INT, segment_no INT
	, wo_id NVARCHAR(40), oper_id NVARCHAR(40), seq_no INT, std_prod_uom_to INT, std_batch_size_to FLOAT, item_id_from NVARCHAR(40), std_item_id_to NVARCHAR(40), actual_prod_rate FLOAT)

DECLARE @bottleneck_rate	TABLE(ent_id	INT, slowest_performance_rate FLOAT, est_prod FLOAT, criteria INT)
DECLARE @perf_rates 		TABLE(child_order INT, slowest_performance_rate FLOAT, est_prod FLOAT, no_of_ents INT, bottleneck_count INT)

DECLARE	 @child_order			INT32
		,@column_position		INT32
		,@curr_column_position	INT32
		,@prod_uom				INT32
		,@batch_size			TFLOAT
		,@std_item_id			NVARCHAR(40)
		,@line_prod_uom			INT32
		,@last_edit_by			STRING80
		,@current_time_utc		TDATETIME
		,@bottleneck_ent_id		INT32
		,@wo_id				STRING40
		,@oper_id			STRING40
		,@seq_no			INT
		,@ent_id			INT

BEGIN
	--Defaults to 0 (no logging).  I.e. a dataset is returned when this SP is called, unless when this SP is called to log the data.
	SET @log_prod_rates = COALESCE(@log_prod_rates, 0)

	SELECT @line_prod_uom = l.prod_uom, @prod_uom = l.prod_uom, @batch_size = l.batch_size, @std_item_id = l.std_item_id, @bottleneck_ent_id = l.bottleneck_ent_id
	FROM line l WITH (NOLOCK)
	WHERE l.line_id = @line_id

	IF (@std_item_id IS NULL) BEGIN
		SELECT NULL ent_id, NULL AS ent_name, NULL AS slowest_performance_rate, NULL AS reas_cd, NULL AS reas_desc, NULL AS state_cd, NULL AS state_desc, NULL AS color
			, dbo.fn_GetWarningMessage(1, @line_id, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL) AS warning
		RETURN
	END

	--Construct the route of line identifying column positions sequentially.
	--Since the child order is not contiguous, use the column position to identify the preceeding column position and the succeeding column position.
	INSERT INTO  @line_route (column_position, prev_column_position, ent_id, child_order, segment_no, can_be_bottleneck)
	SELECT DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY lel.child_order) AS column_position
		--Set the previous column position to identify the previous column position from the current column position
		, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY lel.child_order) -1 AS prev_column_position
		--, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lel.child_order ORDER BY lel.child_order, lel.segment_no) AS col_pos_row_num
		, lel.ent_id, lel.child_order, lel.segment_no, lel.can_be_bottleneck
	FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
	INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = e.ent_id
	--Filter the entities in a line using the supplied line ID.
	WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
	  AND lel.child_order IS NOT NULL
	  AND lel.line_is_child = 0
	ORDER BY lel.child_order, lel.segment_no, e.ent_name

	INSERT INTO @production_rates (column_position, child_order, ent_id, segment_no
					, wo_id, oper_id, seq_no, std_prod_uom_to, std_batch_size_to
					, item_id_from, std_item_id_to, actual_prod_rate)
	SELECT --Identify the jobs running on the column position and/or child order
		 first_col_pos_prod_rates.column_position,  first_col_pos_prod_rates.child_order
		--Identify the jobs running on different entities in a column position.
		, first_col_pos_prod_rates.ent_id
		--If the entity in a line is configured in a segment, identify the segment_no
		, first_col_pos_prod_rates.segment_no
		--Identify the work order, batch size
		, first_col_pos_prod_rates.wo_id, first_col_pos_prod_rates.oper_id, first_col_pos_prod_rates.seq_no
		, first_col_pos_prod_rates.std_prod_uom_to, first_col_pos_prod_rates.std_batch_size_to
		--Identify the from item ID and to item ID
		, first_col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from, first_col_pos_prod_rates.std_item_id_to
		, CASE WHEN job_item.uom_id = std_item.uom_id
				--If the uoms for the from_item_id and to_item_id are the same, then no conversion is required.
				THEN first_col_pos_prod_rates.prod_rate * first_col_pos_prod_rates.batch_size
		   WHEN job_item.uom_id <> std_item.uom_id AND (uc.item_id IS NULL OR uc.item_id = first_col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from)
				--The uoms for the from item id and to item id are differet, and if a conversion is defined in the uom_conv table
				--Use the conversion factor to multiply with the production rates.
				THEN first_col_pos_prod_rates.prod_rate * first_col_pos_prod_rates.batch_size * uc.factor
				--If the item IDs are different and no such conversion is provided, then return -9999999
			ELSE -9999999
	  END actual_prod_rate
	FROM
		(SELECT lr.column_position, lr.child_order, lr.ent_id, lr.segment_no, j.wo_id, j.oper_id, j.seq_no
			--Use the production rate from the running job to convert the production rate to batches/hour
			, COALESCE(dbo.fn_ConvertRate(j.est_prod_rate, j.prod_uom, 3)
				--If a job is not currently running on the entity, then default the production rate from oee_exec
					, dbo.fn_ConvertRate(oee.def_prod_rate, oee.prod_uom, 3)) AS prod_rate
			, COALESCE(j.batch_size, oee.batch_size) AS batch_size
			-- Use the prod uom from line, if that is configured, then use the uom from oee, if not use the job's prod_uom
			, COALESCE(@prod_uom, oee.prod_uom, j.prod_uom) std_prod_uom_to
			--Use the batch size from the line, if not use the batch size from oee, if not use the job's batch size
			, COALESCE(@batch_size, oee.batch_size, j.batch_size) std_batch_size_to
			--FROM ITEM ID: use the item that is produced by the job, if not use the std_item_id from the oee_exec
			, COALESCE(j.item_id, oee.std_item_id) AS item_id_from
			--TO ITEM ID: Use the standard item ID configured for the line, if not, use the item ID for the job; otherwise, use the standard item ID configured in the oee_exec for this entity;.
			, COALESCE(@std_item_id, j.item_id, oee.std_item_id) AS std_item_id_to
		FROM @line_route lr
		INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lr.ent_id = e.ent_id
		--Retrieve the production rate from all the jobs running on an entity.  Only include the jobs that are currently running.
		LEFT OUTER JOIN job j WITH (NOLOCK) ON j.run_ent_id = lr.ent_id AND j.state_cd = 3
		--Join the jobs (j) with the job exec (je) to filter the jobs that are currently running on the line entities in column position 1.
		LEFT OUTER JOIN job_exec je WITH (NOLOCK) ON je.ent_id = e.ent_id AND j.wo_id = je.cur_wo_id AND j.oper_id = je.cur_oper_id AND j.seq_no = je.cur_seq_no
		--Default the data from oee_exec if production rates or uom is not found for an entity (i.e. from a job)
		LEFT OUTER JOIN oee_exec oee WITH (NOLOCK) ON oee.ent_id = e.ent_id
		--Filter the entities to the entities in column position 1.
		WHERE lr.column_position = 1
		) first_col_pos_prod_rates
	--Map the standard item to the item to retrieve the uom_id (TO)
	LEFT OUTER JOIN item std_item WITH (NOLOCK) ON first_col_pos_prod_rates.std_item_id_to = std_item.item_id
	--Map the job's item to the item to retrieve the uom_id (FROM)
	LEFT OUTER JOIN item job_item WITH (NOLOCK) ON first_col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from = job_item.item_id
	--Use the uom_id from the item produced by the job and uom_id identified as the standard item to retrieve the conversion factor
	LEFT OUTER JOIN uom_conv uc WITH (NOLOCK) ON uc.from_uom_id = job_item.uom_id AND uc.to_uom_id = std_item.uom_id
	WHERE (uc.item_id IS NULL OR uc.item_id = first_col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from)

	--Verify whether the standardized item can be identified from the first column position, if not exit.
	IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @production_rates WHERE std_item_id_to IS NULL) OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @production_rates)
	BEGIN
		SELECT TOP 1 @child_order = child_order, @ent_id = ent_id, @wo_id = wo_id, @oper_id = oper_id, @seq_no = seq_no
		FROM @production_rates
		WHERE COALESCE(actual_prod_rate, -9999999) <= 0

		--Since a standardized item cannot be identified, return.
		SELECT NULL ent_id, NULL AS ent_name, NULL AS slowest_performance_rate, NULL AS reas_cd, NULL AS reas_desc, NULL AS state_cd, NULL AS state_desc, NULL AS color
			, dbo.fn_GetWarningMessage(2, @line_id, @child_order, @ent_id, NULL, @wo_id, @oper_id, @seq_no) AS warning
		RETURN
	END

	--Retrieve the standardized units, if the line does have standardized units
	SELECT TOP 1 @prod_uom = COALESCE(@prod_uom, pr.std_prod_uom_to), @batch_size = COALESCE(@batch_size, pr.std_batch_size_to), @std_item_id = COALESCE(@std_item_id, pr.std_item_id_to)
	FROM @production_rates pr

	--Default the current column position to 2, since the column position 1 was already handled in the select statement above.
	SET @column_position = 2

	--Loop through all the column positions (or child orders) in a line.
	WHILE (@column_position IS NOT NULL) BEGIN

		INSERT INTO @production_rates (column_position, child_order, ent_id, segment_no
					, wo_id, oper_id, seq_no
					, item_id_from, std_item_id_to, actual_prod_rate)
		SELECT DISTINCT --Identify the jobs running on the column position and/or child order
			  @column_position, col_pos_prod_rates.child_order
			--Identify the jobs running on different entities in a column position.
			, col_pos_prod_rates.ent_id
			--If the entity in a line is configured in a segment, identify the segment_no
			, col_pos_prod_rates.segment_no
			--Identify the work order, batch size
			, col_pos_prod_rates.wo_id, col_pos_prod_rates.oper_id, col_pos_prod_rates.seq_no --, col_pos_prod_rates.batch_size
			--Identify the from item ID and to item ID
			, col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from, col_pos_prod_rates.std_item_id_to
			, CASE WHEN job_item.uom_id = std_item.uom_id
					--If the uoms for the from_item_id and to_item_id are the same, then no conversion is required.
						THEN col_pos_prod_rates.prod_rate * col_pos_prod_rates.batch_size
				   WHEN job_item.uom_id <> std_item.uom_id AND (uc.item_id IS NULL OR uc.item_id = col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from)
					--The uoms for the from item id and to item id are different, and if a conversion is defined in the uom_conv table
					--Use the conversion factor to multiply with the production rates.
						THEN col_pos_prod_rates.prod_rate * col_pos_prod_rates.batch_size * uc.factor
					--If the item IDs are different and no such conversion is provided, then return -9999999
					ELSE -9999999
			  END actual_prod_rate
		FROM
			(SELECT lr.column_position, lr.child_order, lr.ent_id, lr.segment_no
				, COALESCE(j.wo_id, col_pos_jobs_not_running.wo_id) AS wo_id
				, COALESCE(j.oper_id, col_pos_jobs_not_running.oper_id) AS oper_id
				, COALESCE(j.seq_no, col_pos_jobs_not_running.seq_no) AS seq_no
				--Use the production rate from the running job to convert the production rate to batches/hour
				, COALESCE(dbo.fn_ConvertRate(j.est_prod_rate, j.prod_uom, 3)
						--If a job is not currently running on the entity, then default to the projected job identified from the upstream operation.
						,dbo.fn_ConvertRate(col_pos_jobs_not_running.est_prod_rate, col_pos_jobs_not_running.prod_uom, 3)
					--If a job is not currently running on the entity, then default the production rate from oee_exec
						, dbo.fn_ConvertRate(oee.def_prod_rate, oee.prod_uom, 3)) AS prod_rate
				--Use the batch size from the job, if not use the batch size from oee_exec
				, COALESCE(j.batch_size, col_pos_jobs_not_running.batch_size, oee.batch_size) batch_size
				--FROM ITEM ID: use the item that is produced by the job, if not use the std_item_id from the oee_exec
				, COALESCE(j.item_id, col_pos_jobs_not_running.item_id, oee.std_item_id) AS item_id_from
				--TO ITEM ID: Use the standard item ID configured for the line, if not use the standard item ID configured in the oee_exec for this entity; otherwise use the item ID for the job.
				, COALESCE(@std_item_id, oee.std_item_id, j.item_id, col_pos_jobs_not_running.item_id) AS std_item_id_to
			FROM @line_route lr
			INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lr.ent_id = e.ent_id
			--Retrieve the production rate from all the jobs running on an entity. Only include the jobs that are currently running.
			LEFT OUTER JOIN job j WITH (NOLOCK) ON j.run_ent_id = lr.ent_id AND j.state_cd = 3
			--Join the jobs (j) with the job exec (je) to filter the jobs that are currently running on the line entities in column position 1.
			LEFT OUTER JOIN job_exec je WITH (NOLOCK) ON je.ent_id = e.ent_id AND j.wo_id = je.cur_wo_id AND j.oper_id = je.cur_oper_id AND j.seq_no = je.cur_seq_no
			--Default the data from oee_exec if production rates or uom is not found for an entity (i.e. from a job)
			LEFT OUTER JOIN oee_exec oee WITH (NOLOCK) ON oee.ent_id = e.ent_id
			--Retrieve the list of jobs that are currently running, but scheduled to the entities in the current column position
			LEFT OUTER JOIN (--From non-segment to segment: Handle the case where the segment number in the previous child order is null, and there is a non-null segment number in the current child order position
							--Segment to segment: Or, handle the case where the segment number in the previous child order is not null, and the segment number in the current child order position is not null
							SELECT DISTINCT jnr.wo_id, jnr.oper_id, jnr.seq_no, jnr.item_id, jnr.est_prod_rate, jnr.prod_uom, jnr.batch_size, jnr.target_sched_ent_id
							 FROM job jnr WITH (NOLOCK) -- jobs not currently running
							--Using the list of entities in the current column position, join the entities in the current column to which the jobs are currently scheduled
							 INNER JOIN @line_route curr_col_pos ON curr_col_pos.ent_id = jnr.target_sched_ent_id
							--Using the previous column position, match the segment number to filter out records that have the same work order
							 INNER JOIN @line_route prev_col_pos ON curr_col_pos.prev_column_position = prev_col_pos.column_position
							--Using the existing production rates temp table, map to the previous column position
							 INNER JOIN @production_rates prod_rates_prev_col_pos ON prod_rates_prev_col_pos.column_position = curr_col_pos.prev_column_position
							--Using the previous column position, join with job (table) to retrieve all the jobs that ran on the entities in the previous column position to figure out the earliest started job (work order)
							--from the previous column position. Limit to jobs that are not completed, cancelled or on hold.
							 INNER JOIN job jobs_start_prev_col_pos ON jobs_start_prev_col_pos.wo_id = prod_rates_prev_col_pos.wo_id AND jobs_start_prev_col_pos.oper_id = prod_rates_prev_col_pos.oper_id
								AND jobs_start_prev_col_pos.seq_no = prod_rates_prev_col_pos.seq_no
							-- Exclude the jobs that are currently running and exclude the jobs that are completed.
							 WHERE jnr.state_cd NOT IN (3, 4, 7)
								AND curr_col_pos.column_position = @column_position
								--Non-segment to segment: there are no segments in the previous column position, but there are segments in the current column position
								AND ((prev_col_pos.segment_no IS NULL AND curr_col_pos.segment_no IS NOT NULL)
								--Segment to segment: the previous column position and the current column position have segments, therefore, the segment_no's have to match.
								OR (prev_col_pos.segment_no IS NOT NULL AND curr_col_pos.segment_no IS NOT NULL AND prev_col_pos.segment_no = curr_col_pos.segment_no)
								--Segment to non-segment: Handle the case where the segment number in the previous child order is not null, and the segment number in the current child order position is nul
								OR (prev_col_pos.segment_no IS NOT NULL AND curr_col_pos.segment_no IS NULL
								--Get the job that started first on an entity in the previous column position and limit ONLY to that work order for the projected jobs
								AND (jobs_start_prev_col_pos.wo_id = COALESCE((SELECT TOP 1 j.wo_id
														FROM job j WITH (NOLOCK)
														INNER JOIN @production_rates pr_prev_col_pos ON j.wo_id = pr_prev_col_pos.wo_id
																AND j.oper_id = pr_prev_col_pos.oper_id AND j.seq_no = pr_prev_col_pos.seq_no
														--Limit to the jobs that ran on entities in the previous column position
														WHERE j.act_start_time_utc = (SELECT MIN(j_prev_col_pos.act_start_time_utc)
																	 FROM job j_prev_col_pos WITH (NOLOCK)
																	 INNER JOIN @production_rates pr_prev_col_pos ON j_prev_col_pos.wo_id = pr_prev_col_pos.wo_id
																		AND j_prev_col_pos.oper_id = pr_prev_col_pos.oper_id AND j_prev_col_pos.seq_no = pr_prev_col_pos.seq_no
																	--Limit to the jobs that ran on entities in the previous column position
																	 WHERE pr_prev_col_pos.column_position = @column_position - 1
																	)
														  AND pr_prev_col_pos.column_position = @column_position - 1)
													--If no jobs ran on the previous column position, then select the first (projected) work order
													--from the previous column position.
													, (SELECT TOP 1 pr_prev_col_pos.wo_id FROM @production_rates pr_prev_col_pos
														WHERE pr_prev_col_pos.column_position = @column_position - 1)
													)
									)
								)								--Non-segment to Non-segment: the segment numbers in the previous column position and the current column positions are all null.
								OR (prev_col_pos.segment_no IS NULL AND curr_col_pos.segment_no IS NULL)
									)
								--Match the same work order
								AND prod_rates_prev_col_pos.wo_id = jnr.wo_id
								--Exclude the entities on which there are jobs currently running in the current column position.
							    AND curr_col_pos.ent_id NOT IN (SELECT jr.run_ent_id FROM job jr WITH (NOLOCK)
																INNER JOIN @line_route ccp ON jr.run_ent_id = ccp.ent_id
																WHERE ccp.column_position = @column_position
																--Use the job state running to exclude the entities
																  AND jr.state_cd = 3)
							) col_pos_jobs_not_running ON col_pos_jobs_not_running.target_sched_ent_id = lr.ent_id
			--Filter the set of entities to this column position
			WHERE lr.column_position = @column_position
			) col_pos_prod_rates
		--Map the standard item to the item to retrieve the uom_id (TO)
		LEFT OUTER JOIN item std_item WITH (NOLOCK) ON col_pos_prod_rates.std_item_id_to = std_item.item_id
		--Map the job's item to the item to retrieve the uom_id (FROM)
		LEFT OUTER JOIN item job_item WITH (NOLOCK) ON col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from = job_item.item_id
		--Use the uom_id from the item produced by the job and uom_id identified as the standard item to retrieve the conversion factor
		LEFT OUTER JOIN uom_conv uc WITH (NOLOCK) ON uc.from_uom_id = job_item.uom_id AND uc.to_uom_id = std_item.uom_id
		WHERE (uc.item_id IS NULL OR uc.item_id = col_pos_prod_rates.item_id_from)

		--Get the next highest column position in a line
		SELECT @column_position = MIN(lr.column_position)
		FROM @line_route lr
		--Exclude the column positions that are already identified.
		WHERE lr.column_position > @column_position
	END

	--Verify whether the production rate cannot be identified or the UOM from one item cannot be converted to the UOM of the standard item
	--If yes, return NULL
	IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @production_rates pr INNER JOIN @line_route lr ON pr.ent_id = lr.ent_id WHERE lr.can_be_bottleneck = 1 AND COALESCE(actual_prod_rate, -999999) < 0) BEGIN
		SELECT TOP 1 @child_order = pr.child_order, @ent_id = pr.ent_id, @wo_id = pr.wo_id, @oper_id = pr.oper_id, @seq_no = pr.seq_no
		FROM @production_rates pr
		INNER JOIN @line_route lr ON pr.ent_id = lr.ent_id
		WHERE lr.can_be_bottleneck = 1 AND COALESCE(actual_prod_rate, -9999999) <= 0

		--Since a standardized item cannot be identified, return.
		SELECT NULL ent_id, NULL AS ent_name, NULL AS slowest_performance_rate, NULL AS reas_cd, NULL AS reas_desc, NULL AS state_cd, NULL AS state_desc, NULL AS color
			, dbo.fn_GetWarningMessage(2, @line_id, @child_order, @ent_id, NULL, @wo_id, @oper_id, @seq_no) AS warning
		RETURN
	END

	--Verify whether the production rates ought to be logged.
	IF (@log_prod_rates = 1) BEGIN
		SET @current_time_utc = dbo.fn_StripMilliSecsFromDateTime(COALESCE(@start_time_utc, GETUTCDATE()))

		--Retrieve the user information to store in the last_edit_by field
		EXEC sp_S_DB_Status_GetAudTrailUsr @last_edit_by OUTPUT, NULL

		--Delete the records in the prod_rate_history table to satisfy the following conditions:
		--i) removing a record that was created by the previous transaction (in the same second) will allow the SP to insert the most recent up-to-date record in the prod_rate_history table
		--ii) history records with start_time and end_time with the same value (i.e. started and ended at the same time) are invalid
		DELETE prod_rate_history
		WHERE line_id = @line_id
		  AND start_time_utc = @current_time_utc

		--Log the production rate history information
		;WITH prod_rate_history_enabled
		AS
		(SELECT pr.*
		FROM @production_rates pr
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON pr.ent_id = ue.ent_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
		WHERE COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
		)
		INSERT INTO prod_rate_history (line_id, ent_id, start_time_utc, start_time_local, end_time_utc, end_time_local
			, est_prod_rate, prod_uom, batch_size, std_item_id, last_edit_by, last_edit_at)
		SELECT @line_id, pr.ent_id, @current_time_utc, dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(pr.ent_id, @current_time_utc), NULL, NULL
			, pr.actual_prod_rate, @line_prod_uom, @batch_size, @std_item_id, @last_edit_by, @current_time_utc
		FROM (SELECT DISTINCT prate.ent_id, ROUND(CASE WHEN @line_prod_uom = 3 THEN prate.actual_prod_rate
			--If the actual UOM is not equal to the line's UOM, convert the rate to line's uom.
			ELSE dbo.fn_ConvertRate(prate.actual_prod_rate, 3, @line_prod_uom)
			END, 8) actual_prod_rate
			--FROM prod_rate_history_enabled prate) pr
			FROM (SELECT prslow.ent_id, MAX(prslow.actual_prod_rate) actual_prod_rate FROM prod_rate_history_enabled prslow GROUP BY prslow.ent_id) prate) pr
		--Retrieve the list of most recent records from the prod_rate_history table to compare the changes
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT prh.* FROM prod_rate_history prh WITH (NOLOCK)
						--Retrieve the latest record for each entity in the production rate history table
						--The latest record for each entity is represented by the most recent start_time_utc field
						INNER JOIN (SELECT mr_prh_start.line_id, mr_prh_start.ent_id, MAX(mr_prh_start.start_time_utc) start_time_utc
										FROM prod_rate_history mr_prh_start WITH (NOLOCK)
										--Limit to the entities that are in a line.
										INNER JOIN prod_rate_history_enabled pr_e ON mr_prh_start.ent_id = pr_e.ent_id
										--Limit the prod_rate_history records to the identified line.
										WHERE mr_prh_start.line_id = @line_id
										--Identify the most recent production rate history records for the entities in the line
										  AND mr_prh_start.end_time_utc IS NULL
										GROUP BY mr_prh_start.line_id, mr_prh_start.ent_id
										) most_recent_pr_start ON prh.line_id = most_recent_pr_start.line_id AND prh.ent_id = most_recent_pr_start.ent_id AND prh.start_time_utc = most_recent_pr_start.start_time_utc
						) most_recent_prh ON pr.ent_id = most_recent_prh.ent_id
		-- The are no records in the prod rate history table for this entity
		WHERE (most_recent_prh.line_id = @line_id OR most_recent_prh.line_id IS NULL)
			--The production rate in thie history table is different than the current rate
		   AND (pr.actual_prod_rate <> COALESCE(most_recent_prh.est_prod_rate, -999999999)
			--UOM is different
		   OR COALESCE(most_recent_prh.prod_uom, -99) <> @line_prod_uom
			--Batch size is different
		   OR COALESCE(most_recent_prh.batch_size, -99) <> @batch_size
			--Item is different
		   OR COALESCE(most_recent_prh.std_item_id, 'Dummy Item ID') <> @std_item_id)

		--Close the most recent (not the current) prod rate history information
		UPDATE prod_rate_history
		SET end_time_utc = @current_time_utc
			, end_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(prod_rate_history.ent_id, @current_time_utc)
		--Get the current production rate history information for each entity in the table that are enabled
		FROM (SELECT mr_prh.ent_id, MAX(mr_prh.start_time_utc) start_time_utc
					FROM prod_rate_history mr_prh WITH (NOLOCK)
					INNER JOIN @production_rates pr ON mr_prh.ent_id = pr.ent_id
					WHERE mr_prh.line_id = @line_id
					  AND mr_prh.start_time_utc = @current_time_utc
					GROUP BY mr_prh.ent_id
			  UNION
			  --Retrieve the list of entities that are disabled
			  SELECT lel.ent_id, @current_time_utc AS start_time_utc
			  FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
			--Filter the entities in a line using the supplied line ID.
			LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
			--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
			LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
			WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
			  AND lel.child_order IS NOT NULL
			  --Include the disabled entities to close off the current history records
			  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 0) = 0
			  AND lel.line_is_child = 0
			) most_recent_pr
		--Restrict the update to the set of entities for which there is a new history record
		WHERE prod_rate_history.line_id = @line_id
		  AND prod_rate_history.ent_id = most_recent_pr.ent_id
			--Restrict to the production rate history records that are NOT the current record
		  AND prod_rate_history.start_time_utc < most_recent_pr.start_time_utc
			--Filter the records by end time is null to close the second most recent history records.
		  AND prod_rate_history.end_time_utc IS NULL
	END

	;WITH positions_perf_rates (child_order, slowest_performance_rate, no_of_ents, bottleneck_count)
	AS
		--Start with positions that do not have parallel entities
	(SELECT lel.child_order --retrieve the slowest production rate for each position
			--MIN: The production rate is measured in batches/hour.  Therefore, the fewest number of batches in an hour is the slowest production rate.
			, MIN(COALESCE(production_rates.actual_prod_rate, -9999999)) slowest_performance_rate
			, COUNT(*) -- count the number of entities in the child order
			, SUM(CASE WHEN lel.can_be_bottleneck = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bottleneck_count -- count the number of entities in the child order that can be bottleneck
		FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
		INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = e.ent_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
		--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
		--Retrieve the minimum production rate from this child order - there are no parallel entities in this child order
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT pr.child_order, MIN(pr.actual_prod_rate) actual_prod_rate
						FROM @production_rates pr
						--Temporary fix until a design decision is made
						--Retrieve all the child order positions that are not in parallel
						--If there is more than one job queued to an entity, use the production rate that is the least in the line.
						--Note: the running, cancelled and completed jobs would have been eliminated from the list when the table @production_rates are populated.
						WHERE pr.child_order IN (SELECT lel.child_order FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
									INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = e.ent_id
										--Filter the entities in a line using the supplied line ID.
										LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
										--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
										LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
										WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
										  AND lel.child_order IS NOT NULL
										  --Exclude the disabled entities
										  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
										  AND lel.line_is_child = 0
						GROUP BY lel.child_order HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
						GROUP BY pr.child_order
						) production_rates ON lel.child_order = production_rates.child_order
		--Filter the records by line
		WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
		  --Exclude entities that are parent to the line
		  AND lel.child_order IS NOT NULL
		  --Exclude the disabled entities
		  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
		--Get the production rate for each position in the line.
		GROUP BY lel.child_order
		--Eliminate parallel entities from the list.
		HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
		UNION
		--Retrieve the production rates for each position that has parallel entities assigned to it.
		SELECT lel.child_order
			, SUM(COALESCE(production_rates.actual_prod_rate, -9999999)) slowest_performance_rate
			, COUNT(*) -- count the number of entities in the child order
			, SUM(CASE WHEN lel.can_be_bottleneck = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bottleneck_count -- count the number of entities in the child order that can be bottleneck
		FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
		INNER JOIN ent e WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = e.ent_id
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
		--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
		LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
		--Retrieve the minimum production rate for each entity in this child order - there are parallel entities in this child order
		--MIN: The production rate is measured in batches/hour.  Therefore, the fewest number of batches in an hour is the slowest production rate.
		LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT pr.child_order, pr.ent_id, MIN(pr.actual_prod_rate) actual_prod_rate
						FROM @production_rates pr
						GROUP BY pr.child_order, pr.ent_id
						) production_rates ON lel.child_order = production_rates.child_order AND lel.ent_id = production_rates.ent_id
		--Filter the records by line
		WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
		  --Exclude entities that are parent to the line
		  AND lel.child_order IS NOT NULL
		  --Exclude the disabled entities
		  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
		--Get the production rate for each position in the line.
		GROUP BY lel.child_order
		--Eliminate non-parallel entities from the list.
		HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
	)
	INSERT INTO @perf_rates (child_order, slowest_performance_rate, est_prod, no_of_ents, bottleneck_count)
	SELECT child_order, slowest_performance_rate
		, dbo.fn_ConvertRate(slowest_performance_rate, 3, 5) -- Convert the production rate from batches/hour to batches/second to determine the estimated production
		, no_of_ents, bottleneck_count
	FROM positions_perf_rates

	INSERT INTO @bottleneck_rate (ent_id, slowest_performance_rate, est_prod, criteria)
	--Determine the bottleneck entity and the rates, assuming that a bottleneck entity is not defined for this line.
	SELECT DISTINCT lel.ent_id
			-- Since all the rates are normalized to batches/hour, if the line's UOM is batches/hour, return the rate as it is in line's uom.
			--In either case, divided the number of batches by the batch size of the line
		, ROUND(CASE WHEN @line_prod_uom = 3 THEN ppr.slowest_performance_rate / @batch_size
				--If the actual UOM is not equal to the line's UOM, convert the rate to line's uom.
				ELSE dbo.fn_ConvertRate(ppr.slowest_performance_rate / @batch_size, 3, @line_prod_uom)
		END, 8) slowest_performance_rate
		, ppr.est_prod  -- No conversion required, it is already converted to batches/second for OEE calculations
		, 1
	FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
	INNER JOIN @perf_rates ppr ON lel.child_order =  ppr.child_order
	LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
	--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
	LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
	--Filter the records by line
	WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
		--Make sure to get the position that is closest to the end of the line, incase if there are two identical production rates
	  AND lel.child_order = (SELECT MAX(pr.child_order) child_order
				FROM @perf_rates pr
				INNER JOIN @line_route lr ON lr.child_order = pr.child_order
				--Get the slowest production rate from a line.
				--MIN: The production rate is measured in batches/hour.  Therefore, the fewest number of batches in an hour is the slowest production rate.
				WHERE pr.slowest_performance_rate = (SELECT MIN(spr.slowest_performance_rate)
								 FROM @perf_rates spr
								 INNER JOIN @line_route lr ON lr.child_order = spr.child_order
								 WHERE lr.can_be_bottleneck = 1)
				  AND lr.can_be_bottleneck = 1)
	--Return NULL if any one of the entity has NULL production rate, because there is no reliable way to find the slowest production rate.
	  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @perf_rates WHERE slowest_performance_rate < 0)
	  --Ensure all the entities in this child order position can be part of bottleneck
	  AND ppr.no_of_ents = ppr.bottleneck_count
	  --Exclude the disabled entities
	  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
	  --Use these rates only if the bottleneck entity is not defined for this line.
	  AND @bottleneck_ent_id IS NULL
	UNION
	--Determine the bottleneck entity and the rates, assuming that a bottleneck entity is defined for this line.
	SELECT DISTINCT lel.ent_id
			-- Since all the rates are normalized to batches/hour, if the line's UOM is batches/hour, return the rate as it is in line's uom.
			--In either case, divided the number of batches by the batch size of the line
		, ROUND(CASE WHEN @line_prod_uom = 3 THEN ppr.slowest_performance_rate / @batch_size
				--If the actual UOM is not equal to the line's UOM, convert the rate to line's uom.
				ELSE dbo.fn_ConvertRate(ppr.slowest_performance_rate / @batch_size, 3, @line_prod_uom)
		END, 8) slowest_performance_rate
		, ppr.est_prod -- No conversion required, it is already converted to batches/second for OEE calculations
		, 1
	FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
	INNER JOIN @perf_rates ppr ON lel.child_order =  ppr.child_order
	LEFT OUTER JOIN util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK) ON lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
	--The current reason for an entity must be enabled so that the entity can be used to calculate the performance rates.
	LEFT OUTER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
	--Filter the records by line
	WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
		--Identify the child order that is identified as the bottleneck for this line.
	  AND lel.child_order = (SELECT beco.child_order
	  			FROM line_ent_link beco WITH (NOLOCK)
	  			--Limit the records to the supplied line ID.
	  			WHERE beco.line_id = @line_id
	  			--Limit the entity that is identified as the bottleneck
	  			  AND beco.ent_id = @bottleneck_ent_id)
	--Return NULL if any one of the entity has NULL production rate, because there is no reliable way to find the slowest production rate.
	  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @perf_rates WHERE slowest_performance_rate < 0)
	  --Ensure all the entities in this child order position can be part of bottleneck
	  --AND ppr.no_of_ents = ppr.bottleneck_count
	  --Exclude the disabled entities
	  AND COALESCE(ur.ent_enabled, 1) = 1
	  --Use these rates only if the bottleneck entity is defined for this line.
	  AND @bottleneck_ent_id IS NOT NULL

	-- Verify whether to log performance rates is turned on, if so, log the performance rates
	IF (@log_prod_rates = 0) BEGIN
		--Verify whether there is a bottleneck rate
		IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM @bottleneck_rate) BEGIN
			--Default the child order to null
			SET @child_order = NULL

			IF (@bottleneck_ent_id IS NOT NULL)
				--If the line has a pre-defined bottleneck, retrieve the child order of the entity to determine whether there are any specific problems with this child order.
				SELECT @child_order = lel.child_order
				FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK)
				WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
				  AND lel.ent_id = @bottleneck_ent_id
			ELSE
				--Select the child order from the slowest production rate
				SELECT @child_order = MAX(child_order)
				FROM @perf_rates
				--Get the slowest production rate from a line.
				--MIN: The production rate is measured in batches/hour.  Therefore, the fewest number of batches in an hour is the slowest production rate.
				WHERE slowest_performance_rate = (SELECT MIN(spr.slowest_performance_rate) FROM @perf_rates spr)

			SELECT NULL ent_id, NULL AS ent_name, NULL AS slowest_performance_rate, NULL AS reas_cd, NULL AS reas_desc, NULL AS state_cd, NULL AS state_desc, NULL AS color
				, dbo.fn_GetWarningMessage(3, @line_id, @child_order, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL) AS warning
			RETURN
		END
		ELSE BEGIN
			--Return the performance rates
			; WITH highest_priority_reasons (priority) AS
			--Find the highest priority reason (current reason) from all the entities
			(SELECT MAX(ur.priority)
			 FROM util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK)
			--Limit to the entities that comprise the bottleneck
			 INNER JOIN @bottleneck_rate br ON ue.ent_id = COALESCE((SELECT oe.util_ent_id FROM oee_exec oe WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE oe.ent_id = br.ent_id), br.ent_id)
			 INNER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
			)
			, latest_reas_start_utc (cur_reas_start_utc) AS
			--If there is more than one reason that have the same priority,
			--get the latest reason that have the highest priority
			(SELECT MAX(ue.cur_reas_start_utc)
			FROM util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK)
			--Limit to the entities that comprise the bottleneck
			INNER JOIN @bottleneck_rate br ON ue.ent_id = COALESCE((SELECT oe.util_ent_id FROM oee_exec oe WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE oe.ent_id = br.ent_id), br.ent_id)
			INNER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
			--Limit to the reason(s) that have the highest priority
			INNER JOIN highest_priority_reasons hpr ON hpr.priority = ur.priority
			)
			, bottleneck_reason (criteria, reas_cd, reas_desc, state_cd, state_desc, color) AS
			--For the latest reason that have the hightest priority,
			--retrieve the reason code, reason description, state code, state desc, color
			(SELECT DISTINCT 1, ur.reas_cd, ur.reas_desc, us.state_cd, us.state_desc, us.color
			FROM util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK)
			INNER JOIN @bottleneck_rate br ON ue.ent_id = COALESCE((SELECT oe.util_ent_id FROM oee_exec oe WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE oe.ent_id = br.ent_id), br.ent_id)
			INNER JOIN util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK) ON ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
			INNER JOIN util_state us WITH (NOLOCK) ON ur.state_cd = us.state_cd
			--Limit to the reason(s) that have the highest priority
			INNER JOIN highest_priority_reasons hpr ON hpr.priority = ur.priority
			--Limit to the reason that has the latest start time
			INNER JOIN latest_reas_start_utc lrsu ON lrsu.cur_reas_start_utc = ue.cur_reas_start_utc
			)
			--Return the performance rates
			SELECT e.ent_id, e.ent_name, br.slowest_performance_rate, breas.reas_cd, breas.reas_desc, breas.state_cd, breas.state_desc, breas.color
				, CASE WHEN breas.reas_cd IS NULL THEN dbo.fn_GetWarningMessage(4, @line_id, NULL, e.ent_id, br.slowest_performance_rate, NULL, NULL, NULL)
				       ELSE NULL
				  END AS warning
			FROM ent e WITH (NOLOCK)
			INNER JOIN @bottleneck_rate br ON e.ent_id = br.ent_id
			LEFT OUTER JOIN bottleneck_reason breas ON breas.criteria = br.criteria
			--Order the entities by entity name
			ORDER BY e.ent_name
		END
	END
	ELSE BEGIN
		--Remove the bottleneck_history records from this table for the current time UTC.
		--The current records will be replaced by the new set of records.
		DELETE bottleneck_history
		WHERE bottleneck_history.line_id = @line_id
		  AND bottleneck_history.start_time_utc = @current_time_utc

		-- Close any existing/most recent bottleneck history information that is changed
		;WITH recent_bottleneck (line_id, ent_id, start_time_utc) AS
		(SELECT bhm.line_id, bhm.ent_id, MAX(bhm.start_time_utc) start_time_utc
		FROM bottleneck_history bhm WITH (NOLOCK)
		WHERE bhm.line_id = @line_id
		  AND bhm.end_time_utc IS NULL
		GROUP BY bhm.line_id, bhm.ent_id
		), close_bottleneck_hist (line_id, ent_id, start_time_utc, bottleneck) AS
		(SELECT bh.line_id, bh.ent_id, bh.start_time_utc
		, COALESCE(open_bottleneck.current_bottleneck, 0) -- When the record is not current, then it will be closed
		FROM bottleneck_history bh WITH (NOLOCK)
		INNER JOIN recent_bottleneck rb ON bh.line_id = rb.line_id AND bh.ent_id = rb.ent_id AND bh.start_time_utc = rb.start_time_utc
		OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 1 current_bottleneck
				FROM @bottleneck_rate br
				WHERE br.ent_id = bh.ent_id
				  AND br.est_prod = bh.est_prod_rate
				  ) open_bottleneck
		WHERE bh.line_id = @line_id
		  AND bh.end_time_utc IS NULL
		)
		UPDATE bh
		SET bh.end_time_utc = @current_time_utc
		, bh.end_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(bh.ent_id, @current_time_utc)
		, bh.last_edit_comment = CASE WHEN @last_edit_comment IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(bh.last_edit_comment, '') + '; ' + @last_edit_comment ELSE bh.last_edit_comment END
		FROM bottleneck_history bh
		INNER JOIN close_bottleneck_hist cbh ON cbh.line_id = bh.line_id AND cbh.ent_id = bh.ent_id AND cbh.start_time_utc = bh.start_time_utc
		WHERE bh.line_id = @line_id
		  AND cbh.bottleneck = 0

		--Log bottleneck history information / change in bottleneck entity or change in bottleneck rate on an entity
		;WITH new_bottleneck (ent_id, est_prod, bottleneck) AS
		(SELECT br.ent_id, br.est_prod
			, COALESCE(open_bottleneck.current_bottleneck, 1)
		 FROM @bottleneck_rate br
		 OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 0 current_bottleneck
		 		FROM bottleneck_history bh WITH (NOLOCK)
		 		WHERE bh.line_id = @line_id
		 		  AND bh.ent_id = br.ent_id
		 		  AND bh.start_time_utc = (SELECT MAX(bhm.start_time_utc) FROM bottleneck_history bhm WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE bhm.line_id = @line_id AND bhm.ent_id = br.ent_id)
		 		  AND bh.end_time_utc IS NULL
		 		  AND bh.est_prod_rate = br.est_prod) open_bottleneck
		)
		INSERT INTO bottleneck_history (line_id, ent_id, start_time_utc, start_time_local, end_time_utc, end_time_local, est_prod_rate, last_edit_comment, last_edit_by, last_edit_at)
		SELECT @line_id, nb.ent_id, @current_time_utc, dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(nb.ent_id, @current_time_utc)
				, NULL, NULL, nb.est_prod
				, @last_edit_comment
				, @last_edit_by, @current_time_utc
		FROM new_bottleneck nb
		WHERE nb.bottleneck = 1

		--Close off the current bottlenck history records, if the entities are disabled.
		UPDATE bottleneck_history
		SET end_time_utc = @current_time_utc
			, end_time_local = dbo.fn_TZ_GetLocalDateFromUtc(bottleneck_history.ent_id, @current_time_utc)
			, bottleneck_history.last_edit_comment = CASE WHEN @last_edit_comment IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(bottleneck_history.last_edit_comment, '') + '; ' + @last_edit_comment ELSE bottleneck_history.last_edit_comment END
		FROM line_ent_link lel WITH (NOLOCK), util_exec ue WITH (NOLOCK), util_reas ur WITH (NOLOCK)
		--Limit the records to the identified line
		WHERE lel.line_id = @line_id
		  AND lel.ent_id = ue.ent_id
		  AND bottleneck_history.ent_id = lel.ent_id
		  AND ue.cur_reas_cd = ur.reas_cd
		  --Limit to reasons that are disabled.
		  AND ur.ent_enabled = 0
			--Limit to the bottleneck history records that are not closed yet.
		  AND bottleneck_history.end_time_utc IS NULL
	END
END

CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_S_User_Name_GetFromGroups]
  (@user_id nvarchar(40) ,
   @sids_xml nvarchar(max))
AS
-- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name		-	sp_S_User_Name_GetFromGroups
-- Description		-	Checks if the user is in the User_Name table.  If not, checks if the security mode is set to OS Group.
--						If so, checks to see if any of the SIDs in the supplied XML match the SID of any group in the Grp_Name
--						table.  If so, the user is added to the User_Name table.  Finally the user's entry in the User_Name table
--						is returned.
--						EXAMPLE XML:
--						<sids>
--							<sid id="S-1-1-123"/>
--							<sid id="S-1-1-456"/>
--						</sids>
-- Author			-	Rich Boyle
-- Date Created		-	08/08/2014
-- Version			-	5.0.0.0
--
-- Copyright (c) 2017 Schneider Electric Software, LLC. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Date_Modified  Modified_By      Changes
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- *************************************************************************************************************************
DECLARE	@doc_handle					INT32
DECLARE @lang_id					INT32
DECLARE @last_edit_at				DATETIME

	-- Check if the user is in the User_Name table and if not if the security mode is set to OS Group
	IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM user_name WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE user_id = @user_id) AND
		EXISTS(SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM system_attr WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE attr_id = 405 AND attr_value = '2') BEGIN
		-- We need to check to see if any of the supplied SIDs match an SID in the Grp_Name table.  If so,
		-- the use user is an MES user an should be added to the User_Name table.
		EXEC sp_xml_preparedocument @doc_handle OUTPUT, @sids_xml

		IF EXISTS(SELECT TOP 1 1
			FROM OPENXML (@doc_handle, '/sids/sid',2) WITH (id nvarchar(68) '@id') grp_sids
			INNER JOIN grp_name gn WITH (NOLOCK) ON grp_sids.id = gn.sid) BEGIN
			-- Get the default language for the system
			SELECT @lang_id = CAST(attr_value AS INT) FROM system_attr WITH (NOLOCK) WHERE attr_id = 344
			-- Insert the user into the User_Name table'
			SET @last_edit_at = dbo.fn_StripMilliSecsFromDateTime( GETUTCDATE() )
			INSERT INTO user_name (user_id, encrypt_pw, active, lang_id, failed_logins, auth_method, last_edit_at)
				VALUES (@user_id, @user_id, 1, @lang_id, 0, 2, @last_edit_at)
		END
	END
	-- Now query the user name table for the user.
	SELECT user_name.user_id
			  ,user_name.user_desc
			  ,user_name.encrypt_pw
			  ,user_name.active
			  ,user_name.hourly_cost
			  ,user_name.email_address
			  ,user_name.lang_id
			  ,user_name.def_dept_id
			  ,user_name.last_login
			  ,user_name.last_pw_change
			  ,user_name.auth_method
			  ,user_name.def_lab_cd
			  ,user_name.smtp_server
			  ,user_name.pop3_server
			  ,user_name.email_account
			  ,user_name.email_pw
			  ,user_name.spare1
			  ,user_name.spare2
			  ,user_name.spare3
			  ,user_name.spare4
			  ,user_name.last_edit_comment
			  ,user_name.last_edit_by
			  ,user_name.last_edit_at
			  ,CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), CONVERT(DECIMAL(19, 4), CONVERT(MONEY, user_name.mod_id))) mod_id
			  ,user_name.row_id
	  FROM user_name user_name WITH (NOLOCK)
	WHERE (user_name.user_id = @user_id)

CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_SA_Item_GetItems]
(@filter_option		INT = 0
,@filter		NVARCHAR(4000) = NULL
,@criteria		NVARCHAR(40) = NULL
,@time_zone_bias_value	INT32 = 0
) AS
--- ***********************************************************************************************************************
-- Module Name       - sp_SA_Item_GetItems
-- Description       - Return a recordset filtered by the supplied parameters
-- Author	     - Raghu
-- Date Created      - 03/31/2006
-- Version           - 3.1.13
--
-- Copyright (c) 2017 Schneider Electric Software, LLC. All rights reserved.
--
-- THIS CODE AND INFORMATION ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY
-- KIND, EITHER EXPRESSED OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE
-- IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND/OR FITNESS FOR A
-- PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
-- Filter	     -
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Date_Modified  Modified_By	Ver	Changes
--05/05/2006	Raghu		3.1.15	HD# 8173, 8174, Supply time_zone_bias_value to sp_SA_GetTempSQLByFilter
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- ***********************************************************************************************************************
SET NOCOUNT ON
SET XACT_ABORT ON
BEGIN

DECLARE  @sSQL			NVARCHAR(4000)
	,@temp_filter		NVARCHAR(4000)
	,@temp_SQL		NVARCHAR(4000)
	,@sSQLWhere		NVARCHAR(4000)
	,@param_def		NVARCHAR(4000)
	,@value			NVARCHAR(80)
	,@start			INT
	,@end			INT
	,@disp_order		NVARCHAR(2)
	,@item_class_id		NVARCHAR(400)
	,@item_class_desc	NVARCHAR(400)
	,@ic_produced		BIT
	,@ic_consumed		BIT
	,@ic_obsolete		BIT
	,@item_id			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@item_desc			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@uom_desc			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@uom_id			INT
	,@template			BIT
	,@lifetime			INT
	,@unit_cost			FLOAT
	,@i_obsolete		BIT
	,@num_decimals		INT
	,@spare1			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@spare2			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@spare3			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@spare4			NVARCHAR(400)
	,@separator			NVARCHAR(2)
	,@attr_counter			INT
	,@temp_where		NVARCHAR(MAX)
	,@attr_value		NVARCHAR(MAX)
	,@pos INT
	CREATE TABLE #attr_filter (filter_count INT, attr_id INT, attr_value NVARCHAR(100))

	SET @time_zone_bias_value = ISNULL( @time_zone_bias_value, 0 )
	SET @separator = '$$'
	SET @attr_counter = 1

	IF (@filter_option IS NULL) SET @filter_option = 0
	IF (@criteria IS NULL) SET @criteria = ''

	IF (@filter_option = 0) BEGIN
		SET @sSQL = 'SELECT ic.item_class_id,ic.item_class_desc,ic.obsolete ic_obsolete,ic.produced,ic.consumed'
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_id,i.item_desc,i.obsolete i_obsolete,i.template '
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'FROM item_class ic WITH (NOLOCK) '
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'LEFT JOIN item i WITH (NOLOCK) ON i.item_class_id=ic.item_class_id '
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'LEFT JOIN uom uom WITH (NOLOCK) ON i.uom_id = uom.uom_id '
		SET @sSQLWhere = ' WHERE (1=1) '
	END

	SELECT @temp_filter = '', @temp_SQL = ''

	IF (@filter IS NOT NULL) BEGIN
		SET @start = 1
		SET @end = 0
		SET @start = CHARINDEX('ICF:', @filter, @start)
		IF @start > 0 SET @end = CHARINDEX('IF:', @filter, @start) ELSE SET @end = LEN(@filter)
		IF @end > 0 BEGIN
			SET @temp_filter = SUBSTRING(@filter, @start, (@end - @start))
			EXEC sp_SA_GetTempSQLByFilter @temp_filter=@temp_filter, @filter_id='ICF:', @time_zone_bias_value=@time_zone_bias_value, @SQL_OUT=@temp_SQL OUTPUT
				, @item_class_id=@item_class_id OUTPUT, @item_class_desc=@item_class_desc OUTPUT, @ic_produced=@ic_produced OUTPUT, @ic_consumed=@ic_consumed OUTPUT
				, @ic_obsolete=@ic_obsolete OUTPUT
			IF (@temp_SQL <> '')
				SET @sSQLWhere = @sSQLWhere + @temp_SQL

			SET @temp_SQL = ''
			SET @start = CHARINDEX('ICA:$$($$', @temp_filter, 1)  --Get Attribute ( starting position
			IF @start > 0 BEGIN
				SET @start = @start + 4 -- Get rid of ICA:
				SET @end = CHARINDEX('$$)$$', @temp_filter, @start)
				IF @end = 0 SET @end = LEN(@temp_filter) ELSE SET @end = @end + 5
			END
			ELSE SET @end = 0	-- Get Attribute ) End Position
			IF @end > 0 BEGIN
				SET @temp_filter = SUBSTRING(@temp_filter, @start, (@end - @start))	-- temp_filter contains set of attribute conditions
				SET @start = 8	-- Starting position of attribute
				SET @end = CHARINDEX(@separator, @temp_filter, @start)	--End position of the first attribute
				WHILE (@end > 0) BEGIN
					SET @temp_WHERE = SUBSTRING(@temp_filter, @start, (@end - @start))	-- Attribute: eg: 1000=jack
					SET @pos = CHARINDEX('=', @temp_WHERE)	--Get = position to split left and right
					SET @value = REPLACE(@temp_WHERE, LEFT(@temp_WHERE, @pos), '')

					IF @value <> '' BEGIN
						INSERT INTO #attr_filter VALUES(@attr_counter, CAST(LEFT(@temp_WHERE, @pos - 1) AS INT), UPPER(@value))

						SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ' JOIN #attr_filter af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + ' ON af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.filter_count = ' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10))
						SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ' JOIN item_class_attr ica' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + ' WITH (NOLOCK) ON ic.item_class_id = ica' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.item_class_id AND af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_id = ica' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_id AND af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_value = ica' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_value'
						SET @attr_counter = @attr_counter + 1
					END
					SET @start = @end + 4
					SELECT @end = CHARINDEX('$$$$', @temp_filter, @start)
				END
			END
			IF (@temp_SQL <> '')
				--SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'INNER JOIN wo_attr wa WITH (NOLOCK) ON wo.wo_id=wa.wo_id '
				SET @sSQL = @sSQL + @temp_SQL

		END --end of item class filter found ie, filter string >0

		SET @temp_filter = ''
		SET @temp_SQL = ''
		SET @start = 1
		SET @end = 0
		SET @start = CHARINDEX('IF:', @filter, @start)
		IF @start > 0 BEGIN
			SET @end = CHARINDEX('$$)$$', @filter, @start)
			IF @end > 0 SET @end = @end + 5 ELSE SET @end = LEN(@filter) + 1
--				IF @end = 0 SET @end = LEN(@filter) + 1
		END
		ELSE SET @end = 0
		IF @end > 0 BEGIN
			SET @temp_filter = SUBSTRING(@filter, @start, (@end - @start))
			EXEC sp_SA_GetTempSQLByFilter @temp_filter=@temp_filter, @filter_id='IF:', @time_zone_bias_value=@time_zone_bias_value, @SQL_OUT=@temp_SQL OUTPUT, @item_id=@item_id OUTPUT
				, @item_desc=@item_desc OUTPUT, @uom_desc=@uom_desc OUTPUT, @uom_id=@uom_id OUTPUT, @template=@template OUTPUT, @lifetime=@lifetime OUTPUT, @unit_cost=@unit_cost OUTPUT
				, @i_obsolete=@i_obsolete OUTPUT, @num_decimals=@num_decimals OUTPUT, @spare1=@spare1 OUTPUT, @spare2=@spare2 OUTPUT, @spare3=@spare3 OUTPUT, @spare4=@spare4 OUTPUT
			IF (@temp_SQL <> '')
				SET @sSQLWhere = @sSQLWhere + @temp_SQL

			SET @temp_SQL = ''
			SET @start = CHARINDEX('IA:$$($$', @temp_filter, 1)  --Get Attribute ( starting position
			IF @start > 0 BEGIN
				SET @start = @start + 3 -- Get rid of IA:
				SET @end = CHARINDEX('$$)$$', @temp_filter, @start)
				IF @end = 0 SET @end = LEN(@temp_filter) ELSE SET @end = @end + 5
			END
			ELSE SET @end = 0	-- Get Attribute ) End Position

			IF @end > 0 BEGIN
				SET @temp_filter = SUBSTRING(@temp_filter, @start, (@end - @start))	-- temp_filter contains set of attribute conditions
				SET @start = 8	-- Starting position of attribute
				SET @end = CHARINDEX(@separator, @temp_filter, @start)	--End position of the first attribute
				WHILE (@end > 0) BEGIN
					SET @temp_WHERE = SUBSTRING(@temp_filter, @start, (@end - @start))	-- Attribute: eg: 1000=jack
					SET @pos = CHARINDEX('=', @temp_WHERE)	--Get = position to split left and right
					SET @value = REPLACE(@temp_WHERE, LEFT(@temp_WHERE, @pos), '')

					IF @value <> '' BEGIN
						INSERT INTO #attr_filter VALUES(@attr_counter, CAST(LEFT(@temp_WHERE, @pos - 1) AS INT), UPPER(@value))

						SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ' JOIN #attr_filter af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + ' ON af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.filter_count = ' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10))
						SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ' JOIN item_attr ia' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + ' WITH (NOLOCK) ON i.item_id = ia' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.item_id AND af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_id = ia' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_id AND af' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_value = ia' + CAST(@attr_counter AS NVARCHAR(10)) + '.attr_value'
						SET @attr_counter = @attr_counter + 1
					END
					SET @start = @end + 4
					SELECT @end = CHARINDEX('$$$$', @temp_filter, @start)
				END
			END

			IF (@temp_SQL <> '') BEGIN
				SET @sSQL = @sSQL + @temp_SQL
			END
		END --end of job filter found ie, filter string >0*/
	END

	SET @sSQL = @sSQL + @sSQLWhere + ' ORDER BY '
	SELECT @disp_order = attr_value FROM system_attr WHERE attr_id = 208 	--208 - Item_Class display order
	IF (@disp_order = '0')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'ic.item_class_id'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '1')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'ic.item_class_desc'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '2')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'ic.item_class_id,ic.item_class_desc'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '3')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'ic.item_class_desc,ic.item_class_id'
	ELSE SET @sSQL = @sSQL + 'ic.item_class_id'

	SET @disp_order = NULL
	SELECT @disp_order = attr_value FROM system_attr WHERE attr_id = 210	--210 - Item Display order
	IF (@disp_order = '0')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_id'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '1')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_desc'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '2')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_id,i.item_desc'
	ELSE IF (@disp_order = '3')
		SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_desc,i.item_id'
	ELSE SET @sSQL = @sSQL + ',i.item_id'

	SET @param_def = '@item_class_id NVARCHAR(400),@item_class_desc NVARCHAR(400),@ic_produced BIT,@ic_consumed BIT,@ic_obsolete BIT,@item_id NVARCHAR(400),@item_desc NVARCHAR(400),@uom_desc NVARCHAR(400)'
	SET @param_def = @param_def + ',@uom_id INT,@template BIT,@lifetime INT,@unit_cost FLOAT,@i_obsolete BIT,@num_decimals INT,@spare1 NVARCHAR(400),@spare2 NVARCHAR(400),@spare3 NVARCHAR(400),@spare4 NVARCHAR(400)'

--print @sSQL
	EXEC SP_EXECUTESQL @sSQL, @param_def, @item_class_id, @item_class_desc, @ic_produced, @ic_consumed, @ic_obsolete, @item_id, @item_desc, @uom_desc, @uom_id, @template
		, @lifetime, @unit_cost, @i_obsolete, @num_decimals, @spare1, @spare2, @spare3, @spare4

	DROP TABLE #attr_filter
END

/*
-- ===========================================================================================
-- Name:  [sp_U_ofi_aut_int_buff_LPR_PostProcessing]
-- Description: Used to process the Label Print Request (Post-Processing)
--
--  JOB LPR - AUT to MES (Post: MES reply to DCS / Feedback)
--
--	STEPS:
--	1 - Get current Job information: job oper_id, job_pos
--  2 - Calculate Entity Name
--  3 - Insert record on JOB_OUT interface (Feedback to DCS with Command 10)
--
--	FINISHED...
--
-- Usage: For AUT interface to post-process the LPR object towards the JOB_OUT interface
-- ===========================================================================================
-- Version	Author  Date (yyyy-MM-dd) 	Change description
-- 0.01.00	XPM, AML   2026-03-02   	Initial version based on JRSU PostProcessing.
-- ===========================================================================================*/
CREATE   PROCEDURE [dbo].[sp_U_ofi_aut_int_buff_LPR_PostProcessing]
	@object_name NVARCHAR(60),
	@interface_type NVARCHAR(15) = 'LPR',
	@ID INT = 0,
	@row_id_output INT = -1 OUTPUT -- row ID -1 means not to be marked
AS
BEGIN
	SET NOCOUNT ON;
	SET XACT_ABORT OFF;

	DECLARE @ID_local INT = -1, 
			@ID_LPR_local INT = @ID,
			@Data_local NVARCHAR(4000) = '',
			@Error_local INT = 0

	DECLARE @TranCounter INT = @@TRANCOUNT;
	DECLARE @TranName NVARCHAR(32) =  RIGHT(CAST(OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID) AS NVARCHAR(50)),23)+ FORMAT(GETDATE(), 'HHmmssfff');
    DECLARE @SavePointName NVARCHAR(32) =  RIGHT(@TranName,29) + N'_' + CAST(@@NESTLEVEL AS NVARCHAR(3));

	SET @row_id_output = -1

	BEGIN TRY
		
		IF @TranCounter = 0
			BEGIN TRANSACTION @TranName;
		ELSE
			SAVE TRANSACTION @SavePointName;

		EXEC [dbo].[sp_S_ofi_aut_int_buff_GetByID]
			@ObjectName = @object_name,
			@InterfaceType = @interface_type,
			@ID = @ID_LPR_local,
			@Data = @Data_local OUTPUT,
			@ErrorCode = @Error_local OUTPUT;

		IF @Data_local IS NOT NULL AND @Error_local = 0
		BEGIN

			-- Variables específicas de LPR
			DECLARE @wo_id NVARCHAR(40),
					@seq_no INT,	
					@sublot_no NVARCHAR(40),
					@hu_number NVARCHAR(40) = NULL, 
					@qty FLOAT, 	
					@no_of_prints INT,
					@bag_type INT,
					@recorded_timestamp DATETIME

			-- Split the data field into local variables
			SELECT	 @wo_id = wo_id
					,@seq_no = seq_no
					,@sublot_no = sublot_no
					,@hu_number = hu_number
					,@qty = qty
					,@no_of_prints = no_of_prints
					,@bag_type = bag_type
					,@recorded_timestamp = recorded_timestamp
			FROM OPENJSON(@Data_local)
			WITH (
				wo_id NVARCHAR(40) '$.wo_id',
				seq_no INT '$.seq_no',
				sublot_no NVARCHAR(40) '$.sublot_no',
				hu_number NVARCHAR(40) '$.hu_number', 
				qty FLOAT '$.qty', 
				no_of_prints INT '$.no_of_prints',
				bag_type INT '$.bag_type',
				recorded_timestamp DATETIME '$.recorded_timestamp' 
			);
	
			DECLARE  @mes_parent_name NVARCHAR(80)
					,@mes_parent_ent_id INT
					,@mes_wo_id NVARCHAR(80)
					,@mes_oper_id NVARCHAR(80)

			-- Set the expected parent object
			SET @mes_parent_name = LEFT(@object_name, CHARINDEX('_' + @interface_type, @object_name) - 1)

			SELECT TOP 1 @mes_parent_ent_id = ent_id
			FROM ent e WITH (NOLOCK)
			WHERE e.ent_name = @mes_parent_name

			IF @mes_parent_ent_id IS NULL GOTO Exit_Tree;

			-- Get the MES work order id
			SELECT	 @mes_wo_id = w.wo_id
					,@mes_oper_id = wa.output_operid
			FROM ufn_ofi_mes_aut_orderid(@wo_id,@seq_no,@mes_parent_ent_id) wa
				LEFT OUTER JOIN wo w WITH (NOLOCK) ON w.wo_id = wa.output_woid

			IF @mes_wo_id IS NULL GOTO Exit_Tree;
			IF @mes_oper_id IS NULL GOTO Exit_Tree;

			 DECLARE	
				 @data_wo_state_cd INT
				,@data_job_state_cd	INT
				,@data_job_pos	INT 
				
			SELECT	@data_wo_state_cd = state_cd 
			FROM wo WITH (NOLOCK)
			WHERE wo_id = @mes_wo_id


			IF @data_wo_state_cd IS NULL OR @data_wo_state_cd = 3 GOTO Exit_Tree;

			SELECT	 @data_job_state_cd = j.state_cd
			FROM job j WITH(NOLOCK)
			WHERE j.wo_id = @mes_wo_id 
				AND j.oper_id = @mes_oper_id 
				AND j.seq_no = @seq_no


			IF @data_job_state_cd IS NULL OR @data_job_state_cd IN (1,2) GOTO Exit_Tree;
			ELSE IF @data_job_state_cd IN (4,5,6,7,8,9) GOTO Exit_Tree;

			SELECT @data_job_pos = job_pos 
			FROM job_exec WITH(NOLOCK)
			WHERE ent_id = @mes_parent_ent_id 
				AND cur_wo_id = @mes_wo_id 
				AND cur_oper_id = @mes_oper_id 
				AND cur_seq_no = @seq_no
			
			SET @data_job_pos = ISNULL(@data_job_pos, -1)
			IF @data_job_pos = -1 GOTO Exit_Tree;


			
			DECLARE @job_command_local INT = 10;
			
			Finishing_OK:


			DECLARE @Cur_time DATETIME = GETUTCDATE()
					,@RC INT

			EXECUTE [dbo].[sp_I_ofi_aut_int_buff_InsertJobOutData] 
			   @wo_id = @mes_wo_id
			  ,@oper_id = @mes_oper_id
			  ,@seq_no = @seq_no
			  ,@ent_id = @mes_parent_ent_id
			  ,@job_command = @job_command_local
			  ,@job_pos = @data_job_pos
			  ,@recorded_timestamp = @Cur_time
			  ,@current_timestamp = @Cur_time
			  ,@object_name = @mes_parent_name
			  ,@interface_type = 'JOB_OUT'
			  ,@return_code = @RC OUTPUT
			  ,@row_id_output =  @ID_local OUTPUT
						
		END
		ELSE
		BEGIN
			IF @Error_local <> 0 SET @row_id_output = @ID_local
			ELSE SET @row_id_output = @ID_local
		END

		Exit_Tree:

		SET @row_id_output = @ID_local
		SELECT @row_id_output as row_id_output

		IF @TranCounter = 0 COMMIT TRANSACTION @TranName;

	END TRY
	BEGIN CATCH
	
		DECLARE @error INT, @message VARCHAR(4000), @xstate INT;
        SELECT @error = ERROR_NUMBER(), @message = ERROR_MESSAGE(), @xstate = XACT_STATE();
		
		SET @row_id_output = @ID_local
		SET @TranCounter = @@TRANCOUNT

		SELECT @row_id_output as row_id_output

		BEGIN TRY
			IF @xstate = -1 and @TranCounter = 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION @TranName;
			IF @xstate = -1 and @TranCounter > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION @SavePointName;
			IF @xstate = 1 and @TranCounter = 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION @TranName;
			IF @xstate = 1 and @TranCounter > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION @SavePointName;
		END TRY
		BEGIN CATCH
			SELECT @row_id_output as row_id_output
			RETURN 0;
		END CATCH
	END CATCH
END;
